- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F11 contract: QEMU plugin BBV slice-consume mode. With plugin args
# slice=N,slice_at=K the plugin counts slice boundaries (one per N
# retired insns) and drains at the end of slice index K (0-based). For
# K=2, drain fires at insn 3*N -- the boundary that closes the third
# slice. Lets a caller chain spawn invocations and produce one
# snapshot per SimPoint cluster representative slice.
#
# Test binary: icount_spin.elf (CSR-less, predictable tight loop).
# Plugin must:
#   1. Accept slice= and slice_at= args.
#   2. Drain at insn (slice_at+1)*slice (the END of slice index
#      slice_at, 0-based).
#   3. Exit 200 (drain) before any icount fallback fires.
#
# Required environment (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU    qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN  libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_ELF     CSR-less fixture (default: icount_spin.elf)

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-icount_spin}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

SLICE=1000
SLICE_AT=2                                # 0-based: third slice
ICOUNT_FALLBACK=10000                     # safety upper bound
EXPECTED_MIN=$(( (SLICE_AT + 1) * SLICE )) # = 3000

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-phase-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_OUT=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_OUT" "$QEMU_LOG"' EXIT

truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_OUT,slice=$SLICE,slice_at=$SLICE_AT,icount=$ICOUNT_FALLBACK" \
  >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[plugin_phase_consume]: expected QEMU exit=200, got $RC"
  echo "--- qemu log ---"
  cat "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_OUT" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[plugin_phase_consume]: state file is empty"
  exit 1
fi

# Verify drain timing via the plugin's own slice counter, not minstret
# (which is a cycle-counter proxy on andes-ax45mpv). At drain the plugin
# logs `idx=N target=K`; for slice_at=K, N must be K+1 (slices fully
# retired). slice_at=2 -> idx=3.
EXPECTED_IDX=$((SLICE_AT + 1))
if ! grep -qE "slice-consume drain \(idx=$EXPECTED_IDX target=$SLICE_AT\)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
  echo "FAIL[plugin_phase_consume]: did not find drain at idx=$EXPECTED_IDX target=$SLICE_AT"
  echo "--- qemu log ---"
  cat "$QEMU_LOG"

152	run_one() {
153	  local mode="$1" name="$2" cmd="$3" idx="$4" total="$5"

155	  local start end elapsed status rc
156	  start=$(date +%s)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Negative test: a corrupted --resume-from-qemu state file must trigger a
# fail-fast in vsim with a recognizable error message, not a segfault, hang,
# or silent forward run on garbage state.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-handoff_roundtrip}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

BAD_STATE=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$BAD_STATE" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT

# 32 bytes of zeros: shorter than hybrid_state_v1, hits the short-read branch.
dd if=/dev/zero of="$BAD_STATE" bs=32 count=1 status=none

set +e
timeout 10 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$BAD_STATE" >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
RC=$?
set -e

# 0    - silent pass on garbage (BAD)
# 124  - bash timeout fired -> vsim hung (BAD)
# 200  - hybrid handoff exit (BAD: drain ran, state was treated as valid)
# else - any non-zero error path (OK)
if [ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || [ "$RC" -eq 200 ] || [ "$RC" -eq 124 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[rt_corrupt_state]: expected non-zero, non-200, non-timeout exit; got $RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

if ! grep -Eq "short read|bad magic|cannot open" "$SIM_LOG"; then
  echo "FAIL[rt_corrupt_state]: stderr did not match 'short read|bad magic|cannot open'"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[rt_corrupt_state] PASS: vsim fail-fast with rc=$RC"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproduces the SIGTTIN hang of QEMU 2 when vsim is launched from a
# non-foreground process group under a real pty.
#
# Without the spawn_qemu stdin redirect:
#   - timeout(1) places vsim+QEMU 2 in a new pgid that is NOT the pty's
#     foreground group.
#   - QEMU 2's -nographic stdio reads the pty, the kernel delivers SIGTTIN,
#     QEMU 2 stops, vsim's waitpid blocks, the outer timeout fires (rc=124).
#
# With the fix (child stdin -> /dev/null in spawn_qemu): no tty access,
# no SIGTTIN, vsim completes the round-trip normally (rc=3).

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-handoff_roundtrip}"
hybrid_resolve_paths

if ! command -v script >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "skip: script(1) not available"
  exit 77
fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Stub --qemu-binary for rt_gdbstub_timeout: parses `-gdb tcp::PORT` from
# argv, listens on PORT, accepts one connection, then sleeps. Never sends
# the `+` ack vsim's gdbstub session waits for, so the read-side timeout
# in Session::recv_byte must fire.

import socket
import sys
import time

port = None
for i, arg in enumerate(sys.argv):
    if arg == "-gdb" and i + 1 < len(sys.argv):
        spec = sys.argv[i + 1]
        if spec.startswith("tcp::"):
            port = int(spec[len("tcp::"):])
            break

if port is None:
    print("qemu_silent_stub: no -gdb tcp::PORT in argv", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)

s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 1)
s.bind(("127.0.0.1", port))

CLAUDE.md:94:`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between QEMU plugin, vsim, and the handback path. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), and the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr). `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=64` supports VLEN up to 512 bits. # Demo T2: PC symbol-resolve switching mode (M2).
#
# Same round-trip as T1 but the harness resolves
# _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc from the ELF symbol table and

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Demo T5: slice-consume entry (M5) + icount exit (M3) on a CSR-less workload.
#
# Demonstrates that the harness can use DIFFERENT trigger modes for
# the entry and exit of the same vsim window:
#
#   QEMU + plugin: slice=N,slice_at=K -> drains at end of slice K (M5).
#   vsim         : --hybrid-icount M  -> drains after M retired insns (M3).
#
# Workload is icount_spin.elf (CSR-less, predictable tight loop), so neither
# side can use the csrwi 0x7C0 marker. There is no natural QEMU2 exit
# because the workload spins forever; this demo asserts the round-trip
# DRAINS correctly at both ends. M8 is covered by T1 / T2 / T6.
#
# Env (auto-detected with sensible defaults):
#   VSIM_QEMU     qemu-system-riscv64
#   VSIM_PLUGIN   libhybrid_handoff.so
#   VSIM_BIN      sim_<cpu>
#   VSIM_ELF      CSR-less fixture (default: icount_spin.elf)
#   SLICE         insns per slice    (default: 1000)
#   SLICE_AT      0-based slice index for drain (default: 1)
#   ICOUNT_FALLBACK QEMU plugin safety upper bound (default: 10000)
#   VSIM_ICOUNT   insns vsim runs before exit drain (default: 5000)
#   SIMPTS        optional simpts file from T4; if set, slice_at picked
#                 from its first row (first column) instead of SLICE_AT env.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-icount_spin}"
SLICE="${SLICE:-1000}"
SLICE_AT_ENV="${SLICE_AT:-1}"
ICOUNT_FALLBACK="${ICOUNT_FALLBACK:-10000}"
VSIM_ICOUNT="${VSIM_ICOUNT:-5000}"
SIMPTS="${SIMPTS:-}"

# If a SIMPTS file from T4 is provided, pick the first listed slice index.
# Otherwise fall back to SLICE_AT env (default 1).
if [ -n "$SIMPTS" ] && [ -s "$SIMPTS" ]; then
  SLICE_AT=$(awk 'NR==1{print $1}' "$SIMPTS")
  SLICE_AT_SRC="simpts(first row of $SIMPTS)"
else
  SLICE_AT="$SLICE_AT_ENV"
  SLICE_AT_SRC="env SLICE_AT"
fi

MODE_LABEL="Slice-consume entry (M5) + icount exit (M3)"
echo "=========================================================="
echo "Mode: $MODE_LABEL"
echo "Workload: icount_spin (CSR-less tight loop)"
echo "Entry: QEMU plugin slice=$SLICE slice_at=$SLICE_AT (from $SLICE_AT_SRC)"
echo "Exit : vsim --hybrid-icount $VSIM_ICOUNT"
echo "=========================================================="

hybrid_resolve_paths

EXPECTED_QEMU_INSN=$(( (SLICE_AT + 1) * SLICE ))
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-slice-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_Q=$(mktemp)
STATE_V=$(mktemp)
QEMU_LOG=$(mktemp)
VSIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_Q" "$STATE_V" "$QEMU_LOG" "$VSIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

echo "[demo M5 1/2] QEMU + plugin: drain at end of slice $SLICE_AT (insn $EXPECTED_QEMU_INSN)"
set +e
timeout 30 "$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_Q,slice=$SLICE,slice_at=$SLICE_AT,icount=$ICOUNT_FALLBACK" \
  >"$QEMU_LOG" 2>&1
QRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: QEMU expected exit 200, got $QRC"
  tail -20 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_Q" ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: QEMU state file empty"
  exit 1
fi

# Verify drain happened at the slice boundary (plugin logs idx=K+1 target=K).
EXPECTED_IDX=$((SLICE_AT + 1))
if ! grep -qE "slice-consume drain \(idx=$EXPECTED_IDX target=$SLICE_AT\)" "$QEMU_LOG"; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: QEMU drain not at slice boundary idx=$EXPECTED_IDX target=$SLICE_AT"
  tail -20 "$QEMU_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Drained PC must be inside icount_spin loop body (0x100004 / 0x100008).
PC_Q=$(python3 -c "
import struct
with open('$STATE_Q', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek(16); print(hex(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0]))
")
if [ "$PC_Q" != "0x100002" ] && [ "$PC_Q" != "0x100004" ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: QEMU drained pc=$PC_Q not in icount_spin loop"
  exit 1
fi
echo "  QEMU drain: idx=$EXPECTED_IDX target=$SLICE_AT pc=$PC_Q"

echo "[demo M5 2/2] vsim: resume + drain after $VSIM_ICOUNT retired insns"
set +e
timeout 60 "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_Q" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_V" \
  --hybrid-icount "$VSIM_ICOUNT" \
  >"$VSIM_LOG" 2>&1
VRC=$?
set -e

if [ "$VRC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: vsim expected exit 200, got $VRC"
  tail -20 "$VSIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi
if [ ! -s "$STATE_V" ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: vsim state file empty"
  exit 1
fi

PC_V=$(python3 -c "
import struct
with open('$STATE_V', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek(16); print(hex(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0]))
")
if [ "$PC_V" != "0x100002" ] && [ "$PC_V" != "0x100004" ]; then
  echo "[demo M5] FAIL: vsim drained pc=$PC_V not in icount_spin loop"
  exit 1
fi
echo "  vsim drain: after $VSIM_ICOUNT insns pc=$PC_V"

echo "[demo M5] PASS ($MODE_LABEL): both drains inside icount_spin ROI"

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	* Always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something changed.
5	
6	## Repository Overview
7	
8	Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a three-phase round-trip: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain) -> **QEMU2** (restore via gdbstub, continue).
9	
10	Two Git submodules:
11	- `QEMU/` - QEMU fork hosting the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`)
12	- `verilator/` - vsim sources; `hybrid/` subdirs hold the plugin and test fixtures
13	- `tools/simpoint/` - SimPoint 3.2 (UCSD) clustering binary; pinned to upstream `17783e5`
14	
15	Shared ABI lives at `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (not inside either submodule).
16	
17	## Build Commands
18	
19	```sh
20	# Build everything (qemu -> vsim -> plugin -> simpoint)
21	source ./setup.sh
22	
23	# Build individual components
24	./scripts/build_qemu.sh                              # QEMU (configure + make -j64)
25	./scripts/build_vsim.sh                              # vsim (Docker/podman, runs ./build.sh inside container)
26	make -C qemu_plugin QEMU_ROOT=./QEMU  # TCG plugin (out-of-tree)
27	./scripts/build_simpoint.sh                          # SimPoint clustering binary (g++ on host)
28	
29	# Build RISC-V ELF test fixtures
30	make -C tests/fixtures              # all fixtures
31	make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_regs.elf  # single fixture
32	
33	# Clean
34	source ./setup.sh clean [qemu|vsim|plugin|simpoint|all]
35	```
36	
37	**Outputs:**
38	- `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`
39	- `verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium` (or other CPU variant)
40	- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`
41	- `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`
42	
43	`scripts/build_vsim.sh` is Docker-based (podman). It builds an image from `verilator/Dockerfile` (target `env`) then runs `./build.sh` inside it, mounting the repo at `/work` and `include/` as `/include:ro`.
44	
45	## Running Tests
46	
47	```sh
48	# All e2e tests in parallel (auto-detects job count from nproc + /dev/shm headroom)
49	bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
50	
51	# Run with specific options
52	JOBS=4 MODE=csr bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # 4-way parallel, CSR-mode only
53	JOBS=1 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                  # sequential (debug)
54	FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh           # regex filter on fixture name
55	LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs bash scripts/run_e2e.sh    # custom log directory
56	
57	# Unit tests (inside vsim build container)
58	# The container build runs: cmake --build build -j
59	# To run ctest directly after build:
60	#   podman run ... ./build.sh && podman exec ... ctest --test-dir build -L hybrid-e2e
61	```
62	
63	**Important:** on a high-core-count machine (128+ cores) `default_jobs()` computes `min(nproc, /dev/shm_free/256MB)` which can reach 128+. Running that many vsim Verilator processes simultaneously saturates CPU and causes timeouts. Use `JOBS=8` (or lower) as a practical cap: `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.
64	
65	`scripts/run_e2e.sh` exits 0 only when all tests pass. Logs go to a `mktemp` directory under `/tmp`; path is printed at the start of each run. Each test's full output lands in `$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log`.
66	
67	**Manual plugin tests**: `tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh` are QEMU-plugin-only smoke tests. They are run manually during plugin development, not wired into `scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Each script is self-contained (sources `setup.sh` artifacts, runs one leg, asserts on stdout).
68	
69	## Architecture
70	
71	### Three-Phase Handoff
72	
73	```
74	QEMU1 --(state file)--> vsim --(state file + V-scratch mmap)--> QEMU2
75	```
76	
77	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On CSR-write trigger (`csrwi 0x7C0, 0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
78	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
79	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
80	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands.
81	5. **qemu_handback** (`src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp`) - Spawns QEMU2, connects via gdbstub, sends P-packet register writes for GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-regs, then `continue`s.
82	
83	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes only the CSRs that the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret`. The QEMU plugin still drains the full M-mode set (`mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`) plus PMP (64 `pmpaddr` + 16 `pmpcfg`) into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are restored only on QEMU2 via the gdbstub P-packet path in `qemu_handback`. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
84	
85	### Trigger Modes
86	
87	- **CSR mode** (default): Pattern-matches `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (entry) / `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (exit) at retire time. CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on Andes ax45mp.
88	- **PC mode**: ELF symbols `_hybrid_enter_pc` / `_hybrid_exit_pc` resolved at startup; CSR insns are bypassed.
89	
90	Both modes coexist in the fixtures. `TRIGGER_MODE=csr|pc` selects at runtime.
91	
92	### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)
93	
94	`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between QEMU plugin, vsim, and the handback path. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), and the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr). `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=64` supports VLEN up to 512 bits. Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.
95	
96	Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp`.
97	
98	### V-State Transport
99	
100	V data registers (v0..v31) move through a fixed scratch region
101	(`kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` on `-M andes_ae350`) in the shared mmap. vsim drives
102	the transfer via the Debug Module **Program Buffer** while the hart is halted, so
103	benchmark binaries issue no transport code:
104	- `stage_v_to_scratch` copies `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` into the scratch region
105	  before resume; `ResumeDriver` then sweeps `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch into the
106	  regfile (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=true).
107	- At drain, `StateDrain` sweeps `vse8.v v0..v31` from the regfile back to scratch
108	  (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=false); `read_v_from_scratch` lifts the bytes into
109	  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]`.
110	- `qemu_handback` ships them to QEMU2 via gdbstub P-packets by register number.
111	
112	Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m1 (vl=vlenb), which also forces vstart=0 so
113	the unit-stride access covers the whole register. The scratch stride is the
114	compile-time `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` (wire-format per-register span), not the
115	runtime vlenb.
116	
117	V scalar CSR transport (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr):
118	- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS
119	- **Tier B** (Program Buffer): vtype + vl via `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` (direct CSR write to vtype sets vill; vl is read-only; only `vsetvl` restores both atomically)
120	
121	Restore order in `ResumeDriver::resume()` when `HYBRID_FLAG_V` is set:
122	1. `mstatus.VS` (enables V in the hart)
123	2. V-data reload sweep: `vsetvl` e8/m1 then `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch in the
124	   Program Buffer. Runs BEFORE the architectural V-CSR restore (whose `vsetvl`
125	   overwrites the sweep's vtype/vl/vstart) and uses x5/x6/x7 as scratch.
126	3. `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in Program Buffer (stages `vl` in x5, `vtype` in x6 via abstract GPR writes first)
127	4. `vstart` (AFTER vsetvl: vsetvl resets vstart to 0)
128	5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
129	6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)
130	
131	`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` issues the matching `vse8.v` dump sweep
132	LAST, after every architectural read (GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret), so the
133	sweep's clobbers and any counter increments cannot corrupt the drained state.
134	
135	### Test Fixtures
136	
137	All fixtures run on the unified `tests/hybrid/e2e.sh` harness, which
138	sets up an `/dev/shm`-backed shared mmap (128 MB) so memory survives
139	the QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 round-trip. Two fixture families:
140	
141	| Family   | Examples                                                    | Notes |
142	|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
143	| asm      | `handoff_roundtrip`, `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_shared_mem` | no C runtime; don't strictly need shared mmap but use it anyway (~20 ms cost is negligible). |
144	| C-level  | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`   | linked against vsim-demo C runtime. Shared mmap is REQUIRED -- the stack/heap and `main()`'s ra-spill/restore around `csrwi 0x7C0,1` must survive vsim -> QEMU2. |
145	
146	The shared mmap is created with `mktemp -p /dev/shm` + `truncate`,
147	then QEMU is launched with `-object memory-backend-file`.
148	
149	Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`. C-level fixtures link `runtime/{crt0.S, trap.S, handler.c}` plus the Andes toolchain's `-lgloss_vh` (semihosting-backed libgloss), using `rt_c.ld`. V-using fixtures require `-march=rv64gcv`. **Phase-2 rule:** the span between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()` runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall (no `printf`, `fopen`, semihosting ebreak, etc.) -- vsim does not implement semihosting, so any libgloss-routed call inside the ROI traps. Phase 1 and phase 3 print via standard newlib stdio (both QEMUs are launched with `-semihosting-config enable=on,target=native`).
150	
151	### vsim CMake Structure
152	
153	vsim lives entirely in `verilator/`. Key CMake options:
154	- `VSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID` (default OFF) - enables e2e CTest registration
155	- `VSIM_CONFIG_FILE` - CPU YAML (default `config.yaml`)
156	- `VSIM_NO_VERILATOR` - skip Verilator build (assume prebuilt)
157	
158	The hybrid orchestration layer (`src/hybrid/*.hpp`) is header-only and depends only on C++20 standard library + the shared ABI header. SystemC/Verilator are not required for hybrid unit tests.
159	
160	Hybrid unit tests (`tests/hybrid/`) use [doctest](https://github.com/doctest/doctest). They are registered in `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` and run via `ctest`. The `recording_bus.hpp` / `RecordingSession` patterns provide duck-typed test doubles for the DMI bus and gdbstub session without requiring virtual interfaces.
161	
162	## Key Files
163	
164	| File | Purpose |
165	|------|---------|
166	| `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` | Wire-format struct (shared by all three components) |
167	| `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | TCG plugin: drain on trigger |
168	| `verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` | Phase dispatcher |
169	| `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` | DMI state restore (Tier A+B) |
170	| `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` | DMI state capture |
171	| `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` | Spawn QEMU2, gdbstub P-packets |
172	| `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp` | V register transport via scratch region |
173	| `verilator/cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` | CTest registration for all e2e fixtures |
174	| `scripts/run_e2e.sh` | Parallel e2e runner (FIFO job pool, per-test logs) |
175	| `tests/fixtures/Makefile` | RISC-V ELF fixture build (Andes toolchain) |

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" \
  "${VSIM_WARMUP_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
  # F21: when WARMUP_ICOUNT is set, surface the snapshot pair so callers
  # can verify the warmup window without re-parsing the state file.
  # Offsets locked by include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h (F13):
  #   mcycle_at_measure_start@3392, minstret_at_measure_start@3400.
  if [ "${WARMUP_ICOUNT:-0}" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then
    MS_MC=$(read_u64_le 3392 "$STATE_VSIM")
    MS_MI=$(read_u64_le 3400 "$STATE_VSIM")
    echo "[$FIXTURE warmup] K=$WARMUP_ICOUNT mcycle_at_measure_start=$MS_MC minstret_at_measure_start=$MS_MI"
  fi
  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
      exit 1
    fi
    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
  fi
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

1	# Hybrid Simulator User Guide
2	
3	Audience: a new engineer who wants to RUN the Andes hybrid simulator,
4	not study its internals. After this guide you can:
5	
6	1. Build every artifact from a fresh clone.
7	2. Configure QEMU, vsim, and the harness for a workload.
8	3. Pick a switching mode (M1..M5, M8) and run one round-trip end-to-end
9	   with a concrete worked example.
10	
11	For internals, read `docs/HYBRID_OVERVIEW.md`. For per-mode drill-down,
12	read `docs/switching_modes_tutorial.md`.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 0. The one-paragraph mental model
17	
18	QEMU runs the boring parts at MHz. vsim (Verilator + SystemC) runs the
19	small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an
20	`mmap` file. A magic trigger (CSR write, PC, or instruction count)
21	hands control between them. One run is three legs:
22	
23	```
24	   QEMU1  -- state.bin + shared mmap -->  vsim  -- same files -->  QEMU2
25	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)         (fast)
26	```
27	
28	The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
29	leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
30	mode".
31	
32	---
33	
34	## 1. Build and environment setup
35	
36	### 1.1 Host prerequisites
37	
38	Install these on the host once:
39	
40	| Package          | Notes                                                |
41	|------------------|------------------------------------------------------|
42	| `git`            | clone the repo and its submodules                    |
43	| C/C++ toolchain  | clang or gcc; needed by QEMU and the plugin          |
44	| `cmake` >= 3.20  | vsim build                                           |
45	| `ninja`          | vsim default generator                               |
46	| `python3`        | plugin tests, demo scripts                           |
47	| `glib-2.0` dev   | QEMU plugin link line                                |
48	| `pkg-config`     | QEMU configure                                       |
49	| `podman`         | runs vsim builds inside `vsim-env:latest` container  |
50	| Verilator        | auto-detected; set `VSIM_VERILATOR_EXECUTABLE` if needed |
51	| QEMU's own deps  | pixman, slirp, ... see `QEMU/README.rst`      |
52	| RISC-V toolchain | `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,nm,objdump}` (Andes v5d)   |
53	
54	The Andes RISC-V toolchain is needed to build the fixtures and to
55	resolve symbols for PC-mode. The harness scripts default to
56	`/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/.../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`;
57	override with `NM=/your/path/to/nm` if you keep it elsewhere.
58	
59	### 1.2 Clone with submodules
60	
61	```sh
62	git clone --recursive https://gitea.andestech.com/nick/hybrid_sim
63	cd hybrid_sim
64	```
65	
66	If you forgot `--recursive`:
67	
68	```sh
69	git submodule update --init --recursive
70	```
71	
72	Submodules under this repo:
73	
74	| Path             | What it is                                          |
75	|------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
76	| `QEMU/`   | QEMU 9.x fork that hosts the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`) |
77	| `verilator/`   | vsim sources (CMake + SystemC + Verilator)          |
78	| `tools/simpoint/`| SimPoint 3.2 clustering binary (UCSD)               |
79	
80	### 1.3 Per-host config (`config.env`)
81	
82	The repo ships a template `config.env.example` listing per-host paths
83	that cannot live in the build system (notably the Andes RISC-V
84	toolchain root, which `setup.sh` does NOT build).
85	
86	On the first `source ./setup.sh`, the template is copied to
87	`./config.env` (gitignored) so your edits never touch git history. If
88	the toolchain lives somewhere other than the default, edit
89	`config.env`:
90	
91	```sh
92	# config.env
93	HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast540/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-elf-newlib-v5d
94	```
95	
96	The single variable today is:
97	
98	| Variable          | What it points at                                                  |
99	|-------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------|
100	| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`| Toolchain root. `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/` must contain `riscv64-unknown-elf-{gcc,ld,nm,objdump,...}`. |
101	
102	How it propagates:
103	
104	- `setup.sh` sources `config.env`, validates `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/`
105	  exists, and `export`s the variable so all child processes see it.
106	- The fixture `Makefile` (`tests/fixtures/Makefile`) defaults
107	  `TOOLCHAIN` to `$(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)` and aborts with a clear error if
108	  the variable is missing.
109	- The unified `e2e.sh` test harness loads `config.env` itself when run
110	  without prior `source ./setup.sh`, then derives

212	## 2. Configuring the simulator
213	
214	There are four configuration surfaces. Most users only touch the env
215	vars in 2.1.
216	
217	### 2.1 Environment variables (the only ones you usually set)
218	
219	`setup.sh` exports these for you. Override only if your artifacts live
220	somewhere non-default.
221	
222	| Variable        | Default                                          | Used by                  |
223	|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------|--------------------------|
224	| `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN` | From `config.env` (sec 1.3); toolchain root  | Makefile, NM derivation  |
225	| `VSIM_QEMU`     | `build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64`                 | every harness            |
226	| `VSIM_PLUGIN`   | `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so`               | every harness            |
227	| `VSIM_BIN`      | first `verilator/build/sim_*`                  | every harness            |
228	| `VSIM_ELF`      | `tests/fixtures/$FIXTURE.elf`           | harness scripts          |
229	| `SIMPOINT_BIN`  | `tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint`                    | M4 demos              |
230	| `NM`            | `$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm`   | PC-mode symbol resolve   |
231	| `TIMEOUT`       | 60 s (some demos use 120)                        | per-leg `timeout` cap    |
232	| `FIXTURE`       | `rt_shared_mem`                                  | which `.elf` to load     |
233	| `EXPECT_RC`     | 0                                                | expected QEMU2 exit code |
234	| `TRIGGER_MODE`  | `csr`                                            | `csr` or `pc`            |
235	| `JOBS`          | auto-cap on this 128-core host: set to 8         | parallel test runner     |
236	
237	Example: override the QEMU binary for one run:
238	
239	```sh
240	VSIM_QEMU=/opt/qemu-9.0/qemu-system-riscv64 \
241	  bash tests/demos/demo_csr_oneshot.sh
242	```
243	
244	### 2.2 The vsim CPU configuration YAML
245	
246	`verilator/config.yaml` selects which Andes core to verilate. The
247	default is `ax45mpv_premium`:
248	
249	```yaml
250	cpus:
251	  ax45mpv_premium:
252	    cpu_series: 45
253	    rtl_package: ax45mpv_premium
254	    cpp_wrapper: ax45mpv_premium_cpu_cluster_subsystem
255	    config: data/configs/ax45mpv_premium.cfg
256	    config_dir: andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl
257	    config_inc_filter: grep '^`define NDS_'
258	    extra_verilator_flags: --threads 8 --unroll-count 256
259	```
260	
261	Switch CPU by pointing CMake at a different YAML:
262	
263	```sh
264	cd verilator
265	cmake -S . -B build -G Ninja -DVSIM_CONFIG_FILE=my_other_cpu.yaml
266	cmake --build build -j
267	```
268	
269	`-DVSIM_ENABLE_HYBRID=ON` registers the e2e fixtures with CTest;
270	`-DVSIM_NO_VERILATOR=ON` skips Verilator (use a prebuilt model).
271	
272	### 2.3 QEMU plugin args
273	
274	The plugin reads `arg=value` tokens after `-plugin <path>,`. They
275	select WHICH switching mode QEMU1 runs in:
276	
277	| Plugin arg           | Effect                                                                 |
278	|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|
279	| `outfile=PATH`       | REQUIRED. Drained `hybrid_state_v1` is written here.                   |
280	| `enter_pc=0xADDR`    | M2: drain when PC == ADDR. Bypasses the CSR-insn matcher.              |
281	| `icount=N`           | M3: drain on the N-th retired insn (per vcpu).                         |
282	| `bbv_out=PATH`       | M4: emit one SimPoint BBV row per `slice=N` insns into PATH.           |
283	| `slice=N`            | Insns per slice (used by M4 and M5). Must be > 0.                      |
284	| `slice_at=K`         | M5: drain at the end of the K-th slice. Requires `slice=N`.            |
285	| `drain_at_exit=1`    | F14: drain when QEMU exits naturally; overrides `minstret` with a plugin-side per-insn counter. |
286	
287	If no mode arg is given, the default is CSR-insn match (M1): the
288	plugin matches `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` at retire.
289	
290	Example invocation (CSR mode, just the minimal arg):
291	
292	```
293	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=/tmp/state.bin
294	```
295	
296	Example (icount mode):
297	
298	```
299	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=/tmp/state.bin,icount=10000
300	```
301	
302	### 2.4 vsim CLI flags
303	
304	`sim_ax45mpv_premium <elf> [flags]`. The hybrid-relevant subset:
305	
306	| Flag                          | Purpose                                                  |
307	|-------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|
308	| `--resume-from-qemu FILE`     | Read drained state, restore into hart, run from PC.     |
309	| `--handoff-out FILE`          | Drain back into FILE when the exit trigger fires.       |
310	| `--shared-mem-path FILE`      | mmap FILE as RAM (zero-copy share with QEMU).           |
311	| `--shared-mem-size BYTES`     | Size of the shared region. Match QEMU `-m`.             |
312	| `--shared-mem-base HEX`       | Guest physical address where file offset 0 lands.       |
313	| `--qemu-binary PATH`          | After drain, spawn this QEMU as Phase 3 (QEMU2).        |
314	| `--hybrid-exit-pc 0xADDR`     | M2 exit: drain when this PC retires.                    |
315	| `--hybrid-icount N`           | M3 exit: drain after N committed insns (vsim side).     |
316	| `--jtag-port N`               | Open the JTAG bitbang port (e.g. OpenOCD).              |
317	| `--log-level N`               | 0=trace .. 5=critical .. 6=off (default 2=info)         |
318	
319	Defaults for `--shared-mem-base` is `0x80000000` (the QEMU `virt` /
320	`andes_ae350` RAM base). Most users never override it.
321	
322	Run `$VSIM_BIN --help` for the full list (waveform/save/restore are
323	license-gated and off by default).
324	
325	The shared mmaps created by the shell harnesses (`tests/e2e.sh`,
326	`tests/demos/*.sh`, `tests/drivers/*.sh`, `tests/plugin/*.sh`) are
327	hardcoded 128 MiB sparse files under `/dev/shm` (`mktemp -p /dev/shm`).
328

330	
331	## 3. Switching modes - which trigger to use
332	
333	| ID  | Trigger                                | Where        | When to pick it                                                |
334	|-----|----------------------------------------|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|
335	| M1  | `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1` insn match          | QEMU1 + vsim | Default. Your binary can embed `csrwi` markers.                |
336	| M2  | PC equals `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc`    | QEMU1 + vsim | Binary is yours, but you cannot insert CSR markers.            |
337	| M3  | Retired-instruction count              | QEMU1 + vsim | Binary is NOT yours (no CSR/symbol). Use a spin loop / blob.   |
338	| M4  | BBV emit + offline SimPoint cluster    | QEMU1 only   | Phase identification before the real run.                      |
339	| M5  | Drain at end of slice K                | QEMU1        | Replay one cluster representative slice on vsim.               |
340	| M8  | QEMU2 exits naturally via semihosting  | QEMU2        | Always. End-of-program signal.                                 |
341	
342	M1/M2/M3 are the three ways to delimit the ROI. M4/M5 stack on top
343	of them for SimPoint-style phase replay. M8 is automatic.
344	
345	Decision flow:
346	
347	```
348	Can you edit the binary?
349	  yes -> insert csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1 around the ROI -> M1
350	  no  -> Does it export _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc?
351	           yes -> M2
352	           no  -> Use icount  -> M3
353	You want phase-aware replay?  -> M4 + M5
354	```
355	
356	> **Writing a kernel for cycle measurement (M1/M2):** keep the measured
357	> kernel anchored inside the `csrwi 0x7C0,0/1` span -- read its inputs and
358	> write its outputs through memory inside the span, or wrap the kernel in a
359	> `__attribute__((noinline))` function called between the markers. The
360	> markers' `"memory"` clobber pins memory I/O but not register-only compute,
361	> so a kernel that carries live vector values in registers across the
362	> boundary may be hoisted/sunk out of the measured window. See
363	> `tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h`.
364

595	
596	| Symptom                                                | Cause / fix                                                          |
597	|--------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
598	| `skip: ... not built; run 'make' ...`                  | `source ./setup.sh` and `make -C tests/fixtures`            |
599	| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 0`                      | Trigger never fired. Wrong mode / wrong PC / wrong icount value.     |
600	| `QEMU 1 expected exit 200, got 124`                    | `timeout` killed the plugin. Increase `TIMEOUT` or tune the target.  |
601	| `missing _hybrid_enter_pc/_hybrid_exit_pc symbols`     | M2 needs a fixture with those labels. Rebuild or use M1.             |
602	| `vsim drained pc=0x... not in icount_spin loop`        | `VSIM_ICOUNT` too small / wrong fixture for M3.                      |
603	| Whole suite times out under `scripts/run_e2e.sh`               | Set `JOBS=8`. Default 128 saturates a 128-core host.                 |
604	| `[FAIL] [N/M] ... -> /tmp/e2e-XXXX/...log`             | Open that log; it is the full stdout+stderr of the failing leg.      |

1	# Switching-Mode Tutorial and Exercises
2	
3	Status: draft for review
4	Audience: engineer running the hybrid co-simulator for the first time
5	Scope: every switching mode (M1-M5, M8) the repo ships, with copy-paste
6	commands and one exercise per mode.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 0. What "switching mode" means
11	
12	The hybrid simulator runs a program across three phases:
13	
14	```
15	   QEMU1  --(state file + shared mmap)-->  vsim  --(state file + same mmap)-->  QEMU2
16	   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)                       (fast)
17	```
18	
19	A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN each leg drains its
20	state and hands off. The codebase ships six rules (M1-M5, M8). They
21	plug into the same harness; you pick the rule with plugin args and
22	vsim CLI flags. The fixture binary does NOT need to change between
23	rules (one fixture can be driven by several modes).
24	
25	This document teaches one mode at a time, then exercises that
26	combine modes.
27	
28	### Quick map
29	
30	| ID | Name                           | Drain trigger                                   | Used at        |
31	|----|--------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|----------------|
32	| M1 | CSR insn match (default)       | `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (enter) / `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (exit) | QEMU1, vsim    |
33	| M2 | PC symbol resolve              | PC equals `_hybrid_enter_pc` / `_hybrid_exit_pc`   | QEMU1, vsim    |
34	| M3 | icount                         | N retired instructions                          | QEMU1, vsim    |
35	| M4 | BBV profile + SimPoint cluster | Plugin emits 1 row per slice; offline clustering | QEMU1 + tool   |
36	| M5 | slice-consume                  | End of slice index K                             | QEMU1          |
37	| M8 | end-of-program                 | QEMU2 exits via semihosting `SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED`  | QEMU2          |
38	
39	M1/M2/M3 are entry/exit triggers (the "boundary" question).
40	M4/M5 are pipeline stages for the SimPoint flow.
41	M8 is the natural end-of-run signal (always at the tail).
42	
43	---
44

75	## 2. M1 + M8 - CSR insn match (the default path)
76	
77	### What it does
78	
79	QEMU1's plugin pattern-matches the encoding `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` at retire
80	time. On hit it drains state to `outfile` and exits 200. vsim does the
81	same on `csrwi 0x7C0, 1`. CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor write on Andes
82	ax45mp, so the fixture binary embeds these two `csrwi` instructions
83	at the ROI boundaries.
84	
85	M8 is automatic: after vsim hands back, QEMU2 finishes the workload
86	and exits via `SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED` semihosting.
87	
88	### Inputs
89	
90	- Fixture ELF with `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` in its source.
91	  Every C-level fixture (rt_c_v_regs, rt_c_matmul, etc.) has these.
92	
93	### Output
94	
95	- Phase-by-phase log line + final `exit 0`.
96	
97	### Run it
98	
99	```sh
100	cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
101	bash tests/demos/demo_csr_oneshot.sh
102	```
103	
104	Expected last line:
105	
106	```
107	[demo M1] PASS (CSR insn match (M1+M8))
108	```
109	
110	### Drill-down (what the demo does internally)
111	
112	Inside, the demo calls the generic harness:
113	
114	```sh
115	FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs TRIGGER_MODE=csr EXPECT_RC=0 \
116	  bash tests/e2e.sh
117	```
118	
119	The plugin gets `outfile=<state.bin>` and nothing else - that is the
120	M1 default. vsim is launched without `--hybrid-exit-pc` and without
121	`--hybrid-icount`, so its ELF pre-scanner watches for `csrwi 0x7C0, 1`
122	PCs at retire.

140	## 3. M2 - PC symbol resolve
141	
142	### What it does
143	
144	Same round-trip as M1 but the trigger is a PC value (not an opcode
145	match). The harness runs `nm` on the ELF to resolve symbols
146	`_hybrid_enter_pc` and `_hybrid_exit_pc`, then passes:
147	
148	- `enter_pc=0x<addr>` to the QEMU plugin (QEMU1 drains there)
149	- `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x<addr>` to vsim (vsim drains there)
150	
151	CSR-mode matchers are bypassed; the `csrwi 0x7C0, *` instructions in
152	the binary become inert (CSR 0x7C0 is a benign vendor-defined write).
153	
154	This proves you can hand off WITHOUT modifying the source.
155	
156	### Inputs
157	
158	- Same fixture as M1 (`rt_c_v_regs`), but the ELF must define
159	  `_hybrid_enter_pc` and `_hybrid_exit_pc` symbols. The C-level
160	  fixtures all do.
161	
162	### Output
163	
164	- `exit 0`, last log line `[demo M2] PASS`.
165	
166	### Run it
167	
168	```sh
169	bash tests/demos/demo_pc_oneshot.sh
170	```
171	
172	### Drill-down
173	
174	```sh
175	ENTER_PC=$(riscv64-unknown-elf-nm --defined-only \
176	              tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf | \
177	              awk '$3=="_hybrid_enter_pc"{print $1}')
178	EXIT_PC=$(riscv64-unknown-elf-nm --defined-only \
179	              tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.elf | \
180	              awk '$3=="_hybrid_exit_pc"{print $1}')
181	
182	# QEMU plugin arg
183	... -plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,outfile=$STATE,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC
184	
185	# vsim arg
186	... --hybrid-exit-pc 0x$EXIT_PC
187	```
188	
189	### Exercise 2
190	
191	Compare exit values: run the demo with TRIGGER_MODE=csr and again
192	with TRIGGER_MODE=pc on the same fixture. Both must exit 0 and
193	both must drain the same PC. Use:

197	xxd state_pc.bin  | head -4

200	The PC field is at offset 16 (`hybrid_state_v1::pc`). For most

206	## 4. M3 - icount round-trip
207	
208	### What it does
209	
210	Both legs drain on retired-instruction count alone. No CSR, no PC
211	symbol. Suitable for CSR-less workloads (an infinite spin loop, a
212	benchmark you cannot edit, etc.).
213	
214	- QEMU plugin: `icount=N1` -> drain at the N1-th retired insn
215	- vsim: `--hybrid-icount N2` -> drain N2 insns after resume
216	
217	### Inputs
218	
219	- Any ELF; `icount_spin.elf` is the canonical CSR-less fixture.
220	
221	### Output
222	
223	- Both QEMU1 and vsim exit 200 with a non-empty state file. There is
224	  no QEMU2 phase because `icount_spin` spins forever (no natural
225	  semihosting exit).
226	
227	### Run it
228	
229	```sh
230	bash tests/demos/demo_icount_roundtrip.sh
231	```

233	Override targets:
234	
235	```sh
236	QEMU_ICOUNT=20000 VSIM_ICOUNT=8000 \
237	  bash tests/demos/demo_icount_roundtrip.sh
238	```

250	## 5. M4 - BBV profile + SimPoint cluster
251	
252	### What it does
253	
254	QEMU plugin emits one Basic-Block-Vector (BBV) row per slice of N
255	retired insns. The output is a SimPoint `.bb` file. Offline,
256	`tools/simpoint/bin/simpoint` reads it and clusters the rows into K
257	representative phases.
258	
259	This is the SimPoint "profile" pass. It produces:
260	
261	- `simpts` file: 1 line per cluster, `<slice_idx> <cluster_id>`
262	- `weights` file: 1 line per cluster, `<weight> <cluster_id>`
263	
264	Later, M5 replays just those representative slices.
265	
266	### Inputs
267	
268	- Any ELF. CSR-less or not - the plugin emits BBV rows regardless.
269	
270	### Output
271	
272	- `WORKDIR/<elf>.bb`, `WORKDIR/simpts`, `WORKDIR/weights` persist on
273	  disk so that M5 can consume them.
274	
275	### Run it
276	
277	```sh
278	WORKDIR=/tmp/m4-profile \
279	  bash tests/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh
280	```
281	
282	Override the slice and total count:
283	
284	```sh
285	WORKDIR=/tmp/m4-bigger SLICE=2000 ICOUNT=20000 MAXK=4 \
286	  bash tests/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh
287	```
288	
289	Expected rows = `ICOUNT / SLICE`. The demo asserts this.
290	
291	### Drill-down: plugin args
292	
293	```
294	-plugin libhybrid_handoff.so,\
295	        outfile=$STATE,\
296	        bbv_out=$WORKDIR/profile.bb,\
297	        slice=1000,\
298	        icount=10000
299	```
300	
301	`slice` is shared with M5; `bbv_out=` is what activates emit mode.
302	
303	### Exercise 4
304	
305	Run the demo with WORKDIR=/tmp/m4-ex SLICE=500 ICOUNT=10000 MAXK=3.
306	Inspect `simpts` and `weights`. The number of lines in each file
307	must be equal and at most `MAXK`. Sum the first column of `weights`
308	- it should be approximately 1.0 (SimPoint may emit unnormalised on
309	small inputs; the demo prints this sum for sanity-check).

313	## 6. M5 - slice-consume entry
314	
315	### What it does
316	
317	QEMU plugin drains at the end of slice K (0-based), where each slice
318	is N retired insns. This is the SimPoint "replay" entry: you ran M4
319	once, picked phase K, and now you want vsim to start from the END of
320	slice K (the QEMU drain leaves you with exactly that architectural
321	state).
322	
323	Plugin args:
324	
325	- `slice=N` (insns per slice; SAME N as the profile pass)
326	- `slice_at=K` (drain at the end of the K-th slice, 0-based)
327	- `icount=M` (safety fallback - if K is invalid, drain at M anyway)
328	
329	### Inputs
330	
331	- Same ELF as the profile pass. Same `slice=N`.
332	- K from `simpts` (T4 output) OR from env `SLICE_AT`.
333	
334	### Output
335	
336	- State file drained at the slice boundary. PC inside the ROI.
337	
338	### Run it
339	
340	Using M4's output directly:
341	
342	```sh
343	WORKDIR=/tmp/m4-profile bash tests/demos/demo_bbv_profile.sh
344	SIMPTS=/tmp/m4-profile/simpts \
345	  bash tests/demos/demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh
346	```
347	
348	Manual K choice:
349	
350	```sh
351	SLICE=1000 SLICE_AT=3 \
352	  bash tests/demos/demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh
353	```
354	
355	Inside, the demo combines two modes: M5 for entry (QEMU side) and
356	M3 for exit (vsim side, `--hybrid-icount`). They are independent;
357	each side picks its own mode.
358	
359	### Exercise 5
360	
361	Pipeline M4 -> M5 by hand (no demo script):
362	
363	1. Run M4 with `SLICE=1000 ICOUNT=10000 MAXK=2`. Note `WORKDIR`.
364	2. `cat $WORKDIR/simpts` and pick the first cluster's slice index, K.
365	3. Run vsim manually:
366	   - QEMU plugin `slice=1000,slice_at=K,outfile=...`
367	   - vsim `--resume-from-qemu STATE --hybrid-icount 5000 --handoff-out STATE_V`
368	4. Confirm both legs exit 200.
369	
370	This is exactly what `demo_slice_consume_roundtrip.sh` automates.

424	## 8. Switching-mode decision flow
425	
426	When you have a new workload, pick a mode like this:
427	
428	```
429	Is your binary YOURS to edit?
430	  yes -> Add csrwi 0x7C0, 0 and csrwi 0x7C0, 1 around the ROI -> M1
431	  no  -> Continue.
432	
433	Does the binary already export _hybrid_enter_pc / _hybrid_exit_pc?
434	  yes -> Use M2.
435	  no  -> Continue.
436	
437	Do you know an instruction count where the ROI is hot?
438	  yes -> Use M3.
439	  no  -> Continue.
440	
441	You want SimPoint phase-aware replay -> M4 + M5.
442	```

1 # How the Hybrid Simulator Works 2 3 A friendly tour for engineers new to this codebase. 4 5 ## The Problem in One Paragraph 6 7 A pure RTL simulator (`vsim`, built on Verilator + SystemC) is **cycle-accurate**: it tells you exactly how many cycles every instruction takes inside the CPU pipeline. The price is speed: it runs at ~5-9 KHz. Booting Linux, running libc init, and warming up before reaching the actual code you care about can take hours. Meanwhile, QEMU runs the same program **functionally** at MHz speed, but it has no notion of pipeline cycles. 8 9 The hybrid simulator combines them: run the boring parts in QEMU, switch to vsim for the small region of interest (ROI) you actually want to measure, and (optionally) hand back to QEMU to finish. 10 11 ## High-Level Concept 12 13 Five big ideas make this possible: 14 15 1. **Memory is shared, not copied.** Both simulators `mmap` the same backing file (`/dev/shm/...`) as their RAM. When QEMU writes a byte at `0x80001000`, vsim sees it instantly, and vice versa. RAM size becomes irrelevant. 16 17 2. **All architectural state fits in one packed struct.** GPRs, FPRs, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, mtvec, ...), PMP (16 cfg + 64 addr), V scalar CSRs (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, vlenb), and the full V regfile (`v0..v31`, up to 2 KB) all live in `struct hybrid_state_v1` (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`). That struct is the wire contract every component agrees on. 18 19 3. **vsim only refreshes what the ROI can mutate.** vsim restores into the hart only what it needs to run (GPRs + PC + V state); on the way out it drains back only what could have changed (GPRs + PC + V state). Everything else (FP, M-mode CSRs, PMP, V regfile bytes when the ROI doesn't touch them) **passes through unchanged** from the QEMU 1 snapshot to the QEMU 2 restore. This skips ~85+ DMI transactions per handoff. 20 21 4. **The trigger is a magic CSR write or a PC match.** `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` enters vsim; `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` exits it. CSR `0x7C0` is in the user-defined range. A third form, `csrrw rd, 0x7C0, rs1`, decides at runtime based on `rs1`'s value (1 = exit). PC-trigger mode skips the magic CSR entirely - the harness names entry/exit PCs on the CLI. 22 23 5. **Microarchitectural state is thrown away.** Caches, TLB, branch predictor, store buffer - none of it transfers. We accept cold caches at handoff and rely on a "warm-up window" before recording. 24 25 ## State Categories and Their Transport 26 27 The wire struct is uniform; transport per category depends on what QEMU's plugin API and the AX45MPV Debug Module are willing to expose. 28 29 | Category | QEMU 1 -> snapshot | snapshot -> vsim hart | vsim hart -> snapshot | snapshot -> QEMU 2 | 30 |---------------------------------------------------|----------------------|------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|--------------------| 31 | GPRs `x1..x31`, PC | TCG plugin reads | DM Abstract Commands (DPC for PC) | DM Abstract Commands (fresh read) | gdbstub `G` packet | 32 | `mtvec` | TCG plugin | DM Abstract Command | passthrough (not re-read) | gdbstub `P` | 33 | Other M-mode CSRs (`mstatus`, `mepc`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `mcycle`, `minstret`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `satp`) | TCG plugin | passthrough (not written) | passthrough | gdbstub `P` (per `kCsrByName`) | 34 | FPRs `f0..f31` | TCG plugin | passthrough | passthrough | gdbstub `P` (per `hybrid_fpr_names`) | 35 | PMP (16 cfg + 64 addr) | TCG plugin | passthrough | passthrough | gdbstub `P` (each slot) | 36 | V scalar CSRs - `vtype`, `vl` | TCG plugin | DM Program Buffer running `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` | DM Abstract Command (fresh read) | gdbstub `P` | 37 | V scalar CSRs - `vstart`, `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`, `mstatus.VS` | TCG plugin | DM Abstract Command, **with Program-Buffer fallback** if the DM rejects | DM Abstract Command (fresh read) | gdbstub `P` | 38 | V regfile `v0..v31` (up to 2 KB) | TCG plugin | shared-mmap scratch region (`hybrid::kVScratchGpa = 0x80FF0000`); fixture executes `vle8.v` to load | fixture executes `vse8.v` back to scratch; vsim memcpys those bytes into `state.vreg[]` | gdbstub `P` (per V-reg index) | 39 | `vlenb` | TCG plugin | not restored (read-only, fixed by NDS_VLEN) | passthrough (verified, not re-read) | not sent | 40 | Guest memory | -- (in shared mmap) | -- (in shared mmap) | -- (in shared mmap) | -- (in shared mmap) | 41 42 "Passthrough" means: vsim copies the field from the inbound snapshot into the outbound snapshot unchanged. The hart never sees it; the field rides from QEMU 1 directly to QEMU 2. 43 44 ## Trigger Modes 45 46 Two ways to delimit the ROI; pick at runtime via `TRIGGER_MODE=csr|pc`. 47 48 | Mode | Entry into vsim | Exit out of vsim | Source of truth | 49 |------|------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-----------------| 50 | CSR | `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` (or `csrrw rd, 0x7C0, rs1` with `rs1==0`) | `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` (or `csrrw rd, 0x7C0, rs1` with `rs1==1`) | the binary itself | 51 | PC | plugin arg `enter_pc=0x...` (no insn match) | vsim CLI `--hybrid-exit-pc 0x...` (synthetic hit added via `CsrTrigger::add_pc_hit`) | the harness/CLI; binary is unchanged | 52 53 Three handoff kinds (`hybrid_handoff_kind` in `include/hybrid/insn_match.h`): 54 55 - `HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER` - QEMU drains and exits; vsim ignores at retire. 56 - `HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT` - vsim drains and exits; QEMU does not encounter this PC. 57 - `HYBRID_HANDOFF_RUNTIME` - vsim decodes `rs1` from the matched insn, reads its current GPR value, fires only when it equals 1. Lets a single binary parameterize entry vs exit at runtime. 58 59 ## Design Rationale 60 61 **One packed struct is the wire format.** Three components in three languages (QEMU plugin in C, vsim in C++, gdbstub-translation layer in C++) need to agree byte-for-byte on what state means. A C struct in a shared header (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`) is the simplest contract that compiles into all three. Versioning is via `magic` + `version`, with `reserved` bytes for forward growth (vxsat/vxrm/vcsr were added by consuming `reserved` rather than bumping to v2). 62 63 **QEMU 1 -> vsim is file-based, vsim -> QEMU 2 is gdbstub-based.** QEMU mainline is used **as-is** (no patches, no fork). It exposes two relevant extension points: the TCG plugin API can *read* state during execution, and gdbstub `-S` can *write* state before the first fetch. Plugins cannot inject state at startup, and there is no `--load-state-from-file` flag. Each direction picks the only working primitive: the plugin drains to a file out of QEMU 1, and gdbstub `G`/`P` packets seed QEMU 2. The vsim side translates between the file and the RSP packets - QEMU never has to know about `hybrid_state_v1`. 64 65 **Passthrough is the largest performance lever.** A naive design would round-trip every field of `hybrid_state_v1` through DM Abstract Commands - hundreds of DMI transactions. Instead, `HandoffController::set_passthrough_input(snapshot)` keeps QEMU 1's drained state in vsim memory; when the exit trigger fires, `StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough(snapshot)` re-reads only x1..x31 + PC + (when V) the six V CSRs via DM, and merges those over the snapshot. Everything the ROI is *not allowed* to touch (FPRs, M-mode CSRs except mtvec, PMP) flows from QEMU 1 straight into the QEMU 2 gdbstub restore. ROI-mutates-FP would silently lose those changes - that's an explicit, documented limitation, not an oversight. 66 67 **The Debug Module handles most ISA registers; `vtype`/`vl` need the Program Buffer.** GPRs, FPRs, and ordinary CSRs all have abstract-command slots in the AX45MPV DM - one DMI transaction each. `vtype` is the exception: the V spec marks it read-only via direct CSR write because writing it sets the `vill` flag and invalidates the vector unit. The only legal restore for `vtype` + `vl` together is the `vsetvl` instruction, which has to *execute on the hart*. The Program Buffer is exactly that slot: stage `vl` and `vtype` in scratch GPRs (x5/x6), then execute `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in the PB. The GPR loop afterwards overwrites x5/x6, so no leakage. 68 69 **Tier-A V CSRs use Abstract-first with a Program-Buffer fallback.** `vstart`, `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`, and `mstatus.VS` are spec-compliant to direct CSR write, but the AX45MPV DM may reject the abstract path on a given build. `ResumeDriver::write_csr_abstract_or_pb` tries Abstract first, checks `abstractcs.cmderr`, and on failure clears the sticky error and falls back to a one-instruction PB sequence (`csrrw x0, csr, x5`). The fallback is silent and per-CSR, so a partially-implemented DM does not block the rest of the restore. 70 71 **The V regfile rides shared mmap, not the Debug Module.** The RISC-V Debug Spec does not allocate abstract-command slots for `v0..v31`; it leaves V to optional Program Buffer or DPI extensions, and the AX45MPV wrapper does not implement either. Pushing 32 x 64-byte regs through the Program Buffer one element at a time would be both slow and intricate. Since both simulators already share an mmap, we reuse it: vsim copies `state.vreg[]` into a fixed scratch region before `dret`, and the fixture's vsim-phase prologue issues `vle8.v` from that region to load the real V regfile. Drain mirrors: the fixture's epilogue issues `vse8.v` to scratch, and the simulator wrapper reads those bytes back into `state.vreg[]` after `StateDrain` returns. The fixture is aware of the contract; the V regfile reuses the mmap that already exists for general memory. 72 73 **Missing-register tolerance is part of the contract.** A given QEMU build may not advertise every PMP slot, and the DM may not implement every CSR. `apply_state` in `qemu_handback.hpp` silently skips any name not in the discovered RegMap (`try_write_named`); `StateDrain::read_64bit_register` returns 0 and clears `cmderr` when the DM rejects. Failing closed would block bring-up on every QEMU/RTL revision; failing soft keeps the happy path moving and surfaces real bugs at the fixture level. 74 75 ## Architecture Flowchart 76 77 ```mermaid 78 flowchart LR 79 subgraph DISK["Shared backing files"] 80 SHM[("/dev/shm RAM
