Two memory regions live in the shared mmap: 129 130 - `SEED` at `0x80100000` - 16 int32 elements, the input pattern. 131 - `V_SCRATCH` at `0x80FF0000` - 2 KB region, the V regfile transport channel. 132 133 ### What each phase does 134 135 ``` 136 Phase 1 (QEMU 1) Phase 2 (vsim) Phase 3 (QEMU 2) 137 ----------------- --------------------------------- -------------------- 138 seed[0..15] = pattern vle32.v v8..v15, (seed) vse32.v v8..v15, (out) 139 csrwi 0x7C0, 0 vadd.vi v9, v9, +100 verify out matches 140 vse8.v v0..v31, (V_SCRATCH) seed (with v9 +100) 141 csrwi 0x7C0, 1 SEMIHOST_EXIT 0 142 ``` 143 144 ### State that crosses each handoff 145 146 | Boundary | Memory | Fresh-read in vsim | Passthrough through vsim | Fixture-mediated (mmap scratch) | 147 |--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------| 148 | QEMU 1 -> vsim | `SEED` already in shared mmap; vsim sees it instantly | (nothing yet) | Snapshot held by HandoffController; mtvec written by ResumeDriver | `state.vreg[]` (zero) staged into V_SCRATCH | 149 | in vsim | `vle32` reads SEED; `vse8` writes V regs to V_SCRATCH | -- | -- | -- | 150 | vsim -> QEMU 2 | `SEED` unchanged | x1..x31, PC, 6 V CSRs (DM) | FP, M-mode CSRs (except mtvec written above), PMP, vlenb (all from QEMU 1) | `read_v_from_scratch` -> `state.vreg[]` -> gdbstub `P` per V-reg | 151 152 ### What each step proves 153 154 | Step | What it tests | 155 |----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| 156 | Phase 1 fills `SEED` via int32 stores | QEMU 1's RAM backend is the shared file (not a private anonymous mapping). | 157 | `vle32.v v8..v15, (seed)` runs in vsim | **Memory written in QEMU survives into vsim**, AND `mstatus.VS` + `vtype/vl` were correctly re-applied by ResumeDriver (otherwise `vsetvli` would have trapped). | 158 | Phase 3 `vse32.v` + verify pass | **V regfile written in vsim survives into QEMU 2.** The `V_SCRATCH` -> `read_v_from_scratch` -> `state.vreg[]` -> gdbstub `P` chain works. `v9 == seed + 100` confirms the *mutated* value, not zero-init or stale snapshot. | 159 | Final exit code 0 | Full round-trip succeeded: shared memory, fresh GPRs, fresh V CSRs, V regfile, and passthrough fields all delivered intact to QEMU 2. | 160 161 A sibling fixture, `rt_c_v_csrs.c`, exercises the V *scalar* CSR survival in isolation (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr) using the same three-phase shape but no V regfile traffic. 162 163 ## Authoring a Fixture: What to Watch Out For 164 165 You are writing **one** ELF whose code body straddles three execution windows: QEMU 1 (pre-ROI), vsim (the ROI itself), QEMU 2 (post-ROI). Each window exposes a different set of host-call peripherals and accepts a different subset of state mutations. The constraints below are the ones that bite first-time fixture authors. Each rule is followed by the reason it exists. 166 167 ### 1. Phase 2 (vsim) must be syscall-free; phase 1 and 3 (QEMU) get standard newlib 168 169 C fixtures link against the Andes toolchain's virtual-hosting libgloss (`-lgloss_vh`), whose `_write`/`_exit`/`_sbrk`/... all bottom out in the RISC-V semihosting magic triple (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). Both QEMU launches enable semihosting (`-semihosting-config enable=on,target=native`), so the triple is intercepted before reaching `mtvec`. vsim does NOT implement semihosting -- inside the ROI the triple routes to `mtvec` -> `m_trap_entry` -> trap loop. 170 171 | Phase | Standard newlib I/O (`printf`, `fopen`, ...) | RISC-V semihosting magic ebreak | What you can do | 172 |---------|----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------| 173 | QEMU 1 | works (via `-lgloss_vh` -> semihosting) | enabled (`-semihosting-config enable=on,target=native`) | full newlib stdio: `printf`, `puts`, `fwrite`, etc. | 174 | vsim | TRAPS (newlib stdio -> `_write` -> semihosting ebreak -> `mtvec`) | not implemented -> trap loop | **register / memory only**. No `printf`, no syscalls, no `_exit`. | 175 | QEMU 2 | works (same `-lgloss_vh` path) | enabled | full newlib stdio. | 176 177 The runtime (`rt_c_helpers.h`) marks the boundary: 178 179 ```c 180 // ===== QEMU 1 window ===== // printf etc. are fine 181 enter_vsim(); // csrwi 0x7C0, 0 -> hand off to vsim 182 // ===== vsim window ===== // syscall-free: registers + memory only 183 exit_vsim(); // csrwi 0x7C0, 1 -> hand off to QEMU 2 184 // ===== QEMU 2 window ===== // printf etc. are fine again 185 ``` 186 187 The forbidden-ness in phase 2 is transitive: anything that ultimately calls `_write`/`_exit`/`_open`/... (i.e. anything that emits via the libgloss syscall stubs) is out. Pure CPU functions are fine: `vsnprintf` into a buffer, `memcpy`, ``, inline asm including V instructions, `setjmp`/`longjmp`. The pattern for cross-phase output is "compute in phase 2, emit in phase 1 or 3." 188 189 There is no third channel; **plan the phase your I/O goes in.** 190 191 ### 2. Only GPRs / PC / V-state survive vsim mutation 192 193 vsim refreshes only `x1..x31` + PC + (when V is enabled) the six V CSRs out of the hart at the exit trigger. Everything else - **FPRs, M-mode CSRs except `mtvec`, PMP, `vlenb`** - rides along untouched in QEMU 1's snapshot. Concretely: 194 195 - Mutating `f3` inside vsim: QEMU 2 sees QEMU 1's value of `f3`. Silently lost. 196 - Mutating `mscratch`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`, ... inside vsim: silently lost. 197 - Mutating PMP inside vsim: silently lost. 198 - Mutating `mtvec`: lost (vsim writes its own mtvec back in but doesn't drain it; the snapshot wins). 199 200 If your test depends on a non-GPR mutation propagating to QEMU 2, you have to mutate it from the QEMU 2 side instead - e.g. set the value into a memory cell during vsim, then `csrw` from it during Phase C. 201 202 ### 3. The V regfile only round-trips if the fixture cooperates 203 204 `v0..v31` doesn't ride DM Abstract Commands. Vsim memcpys QEMU 1's `state.vreg[]` into a fixed scratch region (`V_SCRATCH = 0x80FF0000`, 2 KB) on resume; the fixture's vsim-phase prologue must `vle8.v v0..v31, (V_SCRATCH)` to load those bytes into the real regfile. Drain mirrors: the fixture's vsim-phase epilogue must `vse8.v v0..v31, (V_SCRATCH)` before the exit trigger, otherwise `state.vreg[]` reaches QEMU 2 with stale (or zero) bytes. 205 206 `rt_c_v_regs.c` is the worked example. 207 208 ### 4. `mstatus.VS` (and `.FS`) must already be set when QEMU 1 drains 209 210 ResumeDriver writes `mstatus` to the vsim hart **only** if the QEMU 1 snapshot has VS bits non-zero (`state.mstatus & 0x600u`). The shared `runtime/crt0.S` runs before the QEMU 1 drain marker and sets `mstatus.VS=Initial` and `mstatus.FS=Initial`. **If you skip the standard crt0**, set both yourself before `csrwi 0x7C0, 0`. Otherwise vsim resumes with `VS=Off` and the very first `vsetvli` in your ROI raises illegal-insn -> trap loop. 211 212 ### 5. The trigger instruction must be 4-byte `csrwi` 213 214 The plugin filters on a 32-bit insn (`size != 4` is rejected). Don't let the assembler emit a compressed form. The runtime helpers wrap the asm in inline strings; if you write the trigger by hand, force `.option norvc` around it. 215 216 ### 6. Stay inside the shared 128 MB RAM window 217 218 Default mmap window: `0x80000000..0x88000000` (QEMU virt's RAM base + 128 MB). The runtime puts: 219 220 - `.text/.rodata/.data/.bss` at `0x80000000` upward (`runtime/rt_c.ld`). 221 - `_stack` at `0x80700000` (override with `-Wl,--defsym,_stack=...`). 222 - `V_SCRATCH` at `0x80FF0000` (must not be touched by your code). 223 - Heap (`_sbrk`) growing from `_end`. 224 225 Anything between `0x80FF0000` and `0x88000000` is yours; above `0x88000000` is unmapped in QEMU 1 unless you also pass a larger `-m`. Below `0x80000000` is MMIO/ROM in QEMU virt and undefined in vsim. 226 227 ### 7. Microarchitectural state does not transfer 228 229 Caches, TLB, branch predictor, store buffer, lr/sc reservations - all dropped at each handoff. Don't rely on a `lr.d` that crosses the entry trigger; it will not see its `sc.d` partner. `mcycle`/`minstret` are not continuous either - keep that in mind if your test reads them. 230 231 ### Where each rule lives in the runtime 232 233 | Concern | File | 234 |-------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------| 235 | Memory map (`_stack`, `_end`, load address) | `runtime/rt_c.ld` | 236 | `mstatus.{FS,VS}` init, sp/gp, `.bss` clear | `runtime/crt0.S` | 237 | M-mode trap save/restore + fatal trap reporter | `runtime/trap.S` + `runtime/handler.c` | 238 | Newlib syscall stubs (`_write`/`_exit`/`_sbrk`/...) via semihosting | `-lgloss_vh` from the Andes toolchain | 239 | Phase markers (`enter_vsim`, `exit_vsim`) | `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h` | 240 | `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc` labels for PC-trigger mode | `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h` (resolved by `scripts/run_e2e.sh` via `nm`) | 241 | QEMU launch flags (`-semihosting-config enable=on,target=native`, `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`) | `tests/hybrid/{roundtrip_e2e,rt_shared_mem}.sh` (QEMU 1), `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` (QEMU 2) | 242 | C-fixture build line (`-nodefaultlibs -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc`) | `tests/fixtures/Makefile` | 243 244 For pure-asm fixtures (`handoff_roundtrip.S`, `rt_all_gprs.S`, ...) the runtime is skipped entirely: link with `handoff_roundtrip.ld` and inline `semihost_exit.inc` for the QEMU 2 exit. Rules 1, 2, 4-7 still apply; you just hand-code the same checks instead of relying on `runtime/`. 245 246 ## Known Limitations 247 248 These are properties of the current implementation that fixture authors hit even when they follow every rule above. Each one has a documented workaround or is on a future-work list. 249 250 ### L1. vsim mutations to FPRs, M-mode CSRs (except `mtvec`), and PMP are silently dropped 251 252 **What this means.** If your ROI executes `fadd f3, ...`, `csrw mscratch, ...`, or modifies any `pmpcfg*`/`pmpaddr*` slot inside vsim, the value reaching QEMU 2 is **whatever QEMU 1 had at the entry trigger**, not what vsim left behind. 253 254 **Affected registers:** 255 - All 32 FPRs (`f0..f31`). 256 - 12 of the 13 M-mode CSRs in the wire struct: `mstatus`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `mcycle`, `minstret`, `satp`. Only `mtvec` is round-tripped. 257 - All PMP entries (16 `pmpcfg`, 64 `pmpaddr`). 258 - `vlenb` (read-only constant; not really a mutation target). 259 260 **Why.** `StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough` re-reads only `x1..x31`, PC, and the six V scalar CSRs via DM Abstract Commands; the rest is copied through from QEMU 1's snapshot. This is a deliberate speed optimisation (~85 fewer DMI transactions per handoff) under the assumption that ROI kernels don't touch FP / M-CSRs / PMP. 261 262 **Workaround.** If your test must depend on a non-GPR mutation, route it through memory: `csrr` the value into a GPR, store to a known address, then `csrw` from that address inside QEMU 2's phase. 263 264 **Permanent fix.** Extend `state_drain.hpp::drain_with_passthrough` to fresh-read the relevant fields via Abstract Commands, mirroring the existing V-CSR block. 265 266 ### L2. Microarchitectural state is dropped at every handoff 267 268 Caches, TLB, branch predictor, store buffer, and **lr/sc reservations** are not transferred. A `lr.d` in QEMU 1 paired with `sc.d` in vsim will not see its reservation. Cycle-accurate measurements taken inside the ROI will see cold caches at entry and again at exit; use a warm-up window before recording. 269 270 ### L3. `mcycle` / `minstret` are not continuous across handoffs 271 272 The cycle and instret counters jump at each transition (each simulator runs them on its own time base). For a monotonic stream, sum across phases manually; treat the gap as a documented discontinuity rather than a bug. 273 274 ### L4. MMIO inside the ROI is undefined 275 276 Touching device registers (UART, PLIC, CLINT, peripheral DMA, etc.) inside the vsim window is unsupported - the cycle-accurate interconnect may not even instantiate the device QEMU 1 was talking to. vsim's only deterministic peripheral is shared memory (the `mmap` backing file); there is no console, no clock, no semihosting. Stick to register-and-memory work inside the ROI. 277 278 ### L5. Self-modifying code across the trigger is not supported 279 280 The magic CSR write is a synchronization boundary by convention. Rewriting code bytes that QEMU 1 has already executed but vsim is about to fetch (or vice-versa) is undefined: caches and translation buffers are dropped, but the underlying mmap is shared, so timing is the only thing keeping you out of trouble. Don't do it. 281 282 ### L6. Single hart only (today) 283 284 The wire struct carries `hart_id` and the plumbing is per-hart-aware, but the resume/drain path has only been exercised on hart 0. Multi-hart fixtures are not yet supported end-to-end. 285 286 ## Where to Look Next 287 288 - `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - the wire contract. 289 - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` - QEMU drain side. See `resolve_handles` (lazy because the dynamic gdb coprocessors aren't registered at vcpu_init) and the entry-trigger callback. 290 - `verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` - passthrough wiring and trigger dispatch. 291 - `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` - GPR/PC/mtvec + V-CSR Tier-A (Abstract w/ PB fallback) + Tier-B (`vsetvl` via PB) restore order. 292 - `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` - DM fresh-read of GPRs/PC/V-CSRs; passthrough merge. 293 - `verilator/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp` - PB exec helper, `encode_vsetvl`, `encode_csrrw`. 294 - `verilator/src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp` - V-scratch staging / drain helpers. 295 - `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` - spawning QEMU 2, RegMap discovery via `qXfer:features:read`, and the `apply_state` template that ships every category to the gdbstub. 296 - `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_regs.c`, `rt_c_v_csrs.c` - the V regfile and V scalar CSR fixtures. 297 - `tests/fixtures/runtime/{rt_c.ld, crt0.S, trap.S, handler.c, rt_c_helpers.h}` - the shared C runtime: linker script, entry, trap reporter, phase-aware drain markers. Newlib syscall stubs come from the toolchain's `-lgloss_vh` (semihosting), not from a project-local libgloss. 298 - `tests/fixtures/Makefile` - per-fixture build rules; documents which `-march`/linker-script combination each tier uses. 299 - `scripts/run_e2e.sh` - run all e2e tests locally without going through CMake/CTest. 300 301 ## Mental Model in One Sentence 302 303 > Two simulators agree on a memory map and a register struct, take turns running the same program, and use a magic CSR write (or a PC match) as the baton-pass. vsim only refreshes the parts the ROI is allowed to mutate (GPRs, PC, V state); everything else rides along in the snapshot from QEMU 1 straight to QEMU 2. 304

1	# Full V-CSR support across the hybrid handoff
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	Today the QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 round trip passes V *register* data
6	(v0..v31) reliably via the `kVScratchGpa` shared-mmap stop-gap, but V
7	*CSRs* are partial:
8	
9	| Component                                    | Out (drain)                          | In (restore)                |
10	|----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------|
11	| QEMU1 plugin (`hybrid_handoff.c`)            | vstart vtype vl vlenb + vreg         | n/a                         |
12	| vsim StateDrain (`state_drain.hpp`)          | x1..x31 + DPC; V CSRs lost           | n/a                         |
13	| vsim ResumeDriver (`resume_driver.hpp`)      | n/a                                  | mtvec only                  |
14	| QEMU2 handback (`qemu_handback.hpp`)         | n/a                                  | vstart + vreg               |
15	
16	Concrete consequences:
17	
18	1. `hybrid_state_v1` has no slots for **vxsat (0x009), vxrm (0x00A),
19	   vcsr (0x00F)**, so the ABI cannot represent the fixed-point flags or
20	   the bundled vcsr alias at any point in the pipeline.
21	2. `ResumeDriver::resume()` (resume_driver.hpp:52-85) restores only
22	   `mtvec`. Per its inline comment, mstatus/vtype/vl/vstart are
23	   "intentionally NOT restored" because vsim DM may silently drop
24	   abstract write of mstatus, and a direct CSR write of vtype sets
25	   `vill=1` per V spec, poisoning the next V instruction.
26	3. `rt_c_v_regs.c:68-72` and `:146-148` work around (2) by re-issuing
27	   `csrs mstatus, t1` and `vsetvli` inside the fixture itself. Every
28	   future V fixture would need to repeat that prologue.
29	4. `StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` (state_drain.hpp:53-61) falls
30	   back on the QEMU1 snapshot for every field except GPRs and PC. If
31	   vsim mutates vstart / vxsat / vxrm / vtype / vl, those mutations
32	   never reach QEMU2.
33	5. `restore_state_via_gdbstub()` only sends `vstart` + the v0..v31 byte
34	   blobs (qemu_handback.hpp:321-332). vtype / vl / vxsat / vxrm / vcsr
35	   are dropped, so QEMU2 boots with stale values from its `-cpu` reset
36	   defaults.
37	
38	Goal: every V CSR survives the round trip transparently. Fixtures stop
39	needing inline `csrs mstatus, ...` or other compensating prologues.
40	
41	## Tiering
42	
43	V CSRs split by writability:
44	
45	- **Tier A - directly writable**: `vstart` (0x008), `vxsat` (0x009),
46	  `vxrm` (0x00A), `vcsr` (0x00F), and `mstatus.VS`. Spec-compliant to
47	  CSR-write directly. DM Abstract path is preferred; Program Buffer is
48	  the fallback when the DM rejects (`cmderr` set).
49	- **Tier B - vsetvli-only**: `vtype` (0xC21), `vl` (0xC20). V spec says
50	  direct CSR write of `vtype` sets `vill=1`; the only correct restore is
51	  `vsetvl x0, rs1, rs2`. Always Program Buffer.
52	- **Tier C - read-only**: `vlenb` (0xC22). Constant from CPU
53	  configuration (`NDS_VLEN`); verify on receive only.
54	
55	Restore order on the vsim side (each step issued via the resume driver):
56	
57	1. mstatus.VS = Initial (Tier A).
58	2. `vsetvl` to re-establish vtype + vl (Tier B).
59	3. vstart (Tier A) - written *after* vsetvl because vsetvl resets vstart
60	   to 0; non-zero values must be restored last to survive.
61	4. vxsat, vxrm, vcsr (Tier A).
62	5. Then the non-V GPR/CSR/PC restore as today.
63	
64	## Critical files
65	
66	| File                                                    | Change                                                                                                |
67	|---------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

69	| `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h`                      | New offset/size static_asserts for the three new fields.                                              |
70	| `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`                          | Resolve + drain vxsat / vxrm / vcsr alongside the existing vstart/vtype/vl/vlenb block.               |
71	| `verilator/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp` *(new)*     | Helper: stage GPR via Data0/1 -> AccessRegister, write progbufN, AccessRegister postexec=1, clear cmderr. |
72	| `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`              | Tier A path with Abstract-first + PB fallback. Tier B `vsetvl` via PB. New helpers `write_csr_via_pb`, `vsetvl_via_pb`. |
73	| `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`                | Read V CSRs via Abstract. Stop relying on QEMU1 passthrough for them.                                 |
74	| `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp`              | Send vtype, vl, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr via gdbstub P packets (extend `kCsrByName` or add a V-CSR list).   |

1	# vsim Semihosting Investigation
2	
3	Scope: can we port QEMU's RISC-V semihosting into the Verilator-based vsim so
4	that binaries linked with `-mvh` (Andes virtual hosting, `libgloss_vh`) can
5	perform I/O system calls on both QEMU and vsim?
6	
7	This document answers step 1 only: how the current vsim handles those system
8	calls today.
9	
10	## Bottom Line
11	
12	vsim does NOT implement semihosting. Every guest syscall trap is fatal.
13	The fixtures work around this with the Phase-2 rule: no libc I/O between
14	`enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
15	
16	## Current vsim Trap Flow
17	
18	1. `libgloss_vh` in the Andes toolchain compiles `printf` / `_write` /
19	   `_exit` / `_sbrk` down to the RISC-V semihosting magic triple:
20	
21	   ```
22	   slli x0, x0, 0x1f    # at mepc - 4
23	   ebreak               # at mepc
24	   srai x0, x0, 0x7     # at mepc + 4
25	   ```
26	
27	2. vsim's hart takes a breakpoint exception at `ebreak` (mcause = 3) and
28	   jumps to `mtvec`.
29	
30	3. `mtvec` points to the fixture's own trap stub:
31	   `tests/fixtures/runtime/trap.S:19-120` saves all GPRs/CSRs and
32	   calls `handle_trap()`.
33	
34	4. `tests/fixtures/runtime/handler.c:23-52` reads `mcause`,
35	   `mdcause`, `mepc`, `mtval` via inline CSR reads, prints
36	   `[ERROR] Trap occurred!` to stderr through libgloss, then calls
37	   `_exit(mcause)`.
38	
39	Critical: `handler.c` never inspects the bytes around `mepc` to recognize
40	the magic triple. The comment at `handler.c:4-6` admits this:
41	
42	> libgloss_vh routes syscalls through the RISC-V semihosting magic triple,
43	> not through `ecall`, so there is no syscall-dispatch table here. Any trap
44	> is treated as a fatal error.
45	
46	That is why CLAUDE.md and `runtime/rt_c_helpers.h:2-9` carry the Phase-2
47	rule: between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()` the fixture must not call
48	any libc I/O function. Phase 1 and Phase 3 print fine because both QEMUs
49	are launched with `-semihosting-config enable=on,target=native`.
50	
51	## Why the Phase-2 Rule Exists in Code
52	
53	- `tests/fixtures/Makefile:22-24` -- comment explaining libgloss_vh
54	  and that "vsim does not implement semihosting."
55	- `tests/fixtures/runtime/rt_c_helpers.h:2-9` -- documents that
56	  inside the span the magic triple would route to mtvec and loop.
57	- `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` -- launches QEMU2 with
58	  `-semihosting-config` so Phase 3 I/O still works.
59	- `verilator/src/main.cpp:114` -- mentions semihosting only as part of
60	  QEMU2 launch docs.
61	
62	Grep across `verilator/` for `semihosting`, `sys_write`, `SYS_WRITE`,
63	`SYS_READ`, `_sbrk` returns no implementation, only those references.
64	
65	## How QEMU Does the Same Thing (Reference)
66	
67	- Detect: `QEMU/target/riscv/insn_trans/trans_privileged.c.inc:28-70`
68	  decodes `ebreak`, reads `[mepc-4, mepc+4]`, matches the triple, then
69	  raises `RISCV_EXCP_SEMIHOST` instead of `RISCV_EXCP_BREAKPOINT`.
70	- Target glue (RV-specific arg/ret regs):
71	  `QEMU/target/riscv/common-semi-target.h:14-26` -- args in `a0/a1`,
72	  return value placed in `a0`.
73	- Dispatcher (around 20 syscalls, ARM Semihosting v2.0):
74	  `QEMU/semihosting/arm-compat-semi.c` and
75	  `QEMU/semihosting/syscalls.c`. Implements `SYS_OPEN`, `SYS_CLOSE`,
76	  `SYS_READ`, `SYS_WRITE`, `SYS_SEEK`, `SYS_FLEN`, `SYS_STAT`, `SYS_ISTTY`,
77	  `SYS_HEAPINFO`, `SYS_EXIT`, `SYS_EXIT_EXTENDED`, and more.
78	
79	RISC-V reuses the ARM Semihosting v2.0 spec verbatim via the magic triple;
80	it is not a RISC-V-specific variant.
81	
82	## libgloss_vh / -mvh Details
83	
84	- `-mvh` is an Andes toolchain flag that selects virtual hosting mode,
85	  routing I/O through the semihosting magic triple instead of through
86	  ecall / proxy-kernel.
87	- `tests/fixtures/Makefile:39-44` link order:
88	
89	  ```
90	  RT_C_LIBS := -Wl,--start-group -lc -lgloss_vh -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
91	  ```
92	
93	- `-lgloss_vh` provides `_write`, `_exit`, `_sbrk`, `_read`, ... built
94	  on the magic triple. Source is not in this repo; it ships in the Andes
95	  toolchain.
96	
97	## vsim Host-Side Hooks Available Today
98	
99	There is no DPI-C bridge, SystemC export, or printf-debug channel from
100	guest to host. The only existing guest-to-host paths are:
101	
102	- The DMI bus (Debug Module) that `ResumeDriver` and `StateDrain` already
103	  use to read and write GPRs / FPRs / CSRs / V-state.
104	- The shared `/dev/shm` mmap region (Tier-2 fixtures) -- the host process
105	  can read it concurrently while the hart runs.
106	- `mtvec` running guest code that the fixture itself controls.
107	
108	vsim's main entry is `sc_main()` in `verilator/src/main.cpp`. It uses
109	`spdlog` and `fmt` for host-side logging; the guest cannot reach those.
110	
111	## Two Natural Integration Points for a Port
112	
113	1. Guest-side, in-trap: extend `handle_trap()` in
114	   `tests/fixtures/runtime/handler.c` to detect the magic triple
115	   (read bytes at `mepc-4` and `mepc+4`), emulate the syscall, write the
116	   result into `a0` in the trap frame, advance `mepc` by 4, and return.
117	   I/O reaches the host via the existing `/dev/shm` mmap (a tail-reader
118	   on the host turns the mmap region into stdout).
119	   - Pros: zero vsim core changes; isolated to the fixture runtime.
120	   - Cons: needs a mmap-based stdio protocol; harder for `SYS_OPEN` /
121	     `SYS_READ` against arbitrary host files; not the same path as QEMU.
122	
123	2. Host-side, over DMI: the `handoff_controller` watches for the
124	   semihosting exception via DMI (same way it already watches CSR
125	   triggers), pauses the hart, reads `a0..a7` via Abstract Commands,
126	   executes the syscall on the host, writes `a0` back, advances `mepc`
127	   by 4, and resumes the hart.
128	   - Pros: architecturally equivalent to QEMU; full POSIX surface
129	     available; no guest-side runtime changes.
130	   - Cons: needs a new trigger path in `handoff_controller` and a new
131	     syscall dispatcher module under `verilator/src/hybrid/`.
132	
133	Next step (not in this doc): pick one of the two integration points and
134	sketch it end-to-end -- syscall list, register-read order, `mepc` fixup,
135	file-descriptor table.

1	# SimPoint-driven hybrid sim: shared-mmap transport vs dump/reload transport
2	
3	Context: extend the existing QEMU + vsim/Verilator hybrid with a SimPoint-driven
4	workflow. End-to-end pipeline:
5	
6	1. **BBV generation** - run the workload in QEMU; emit Basic Block Vectors
7	   (one per fixed-size slice of dynamic instructions) into a `.bb` file.
8	2. **SimPoint clustering** - feed the `.bb` file into the SimPoint tool; it
9	   selects K representative slices and weights.
10	3. **Checkpoint collection** - replay the workload in QEMU, drain a checkpoint
11	   (architectural state + memory image) at each of the K simpoint boundaries.
12	4. **Detailed replay** - for each checkpoint, restore into vsim/Verilator and
13	   collect cycle-accurate metrics. Combine per-region metrics by weight.
14	
15	Steps 3 and 4 are exactly the QEMU -> vsim handoff we already have, just
16	repeated K times at SimPoint-selected boundaries instead of at WFI / CSR write.
17	The transport choice for that handoff matters: per-region snapshot cost
18	multiplies by K (often 10-30), and the trigger surface must accept "fire at
19	instruction count N", not just "fire at this PC".
20	
21	Two candidate transports exist in our tree today:
22	
23	1. The **shared-mmap** transport used by `hybrid_sim/` (this repo).
24	2. The **dump/reload** transport used by `/local/nick/vsim-demo-new/demo/hybrid`.
25	
26	This document compares them and recommends a path.
27	
28	---
29	
30	## 1. Mechanics side-by-side
31	
32	| Aspect | `hybrid_sim` (shared mmap) | `vsim-demo-new/demo/hybrid` (dump/reload) |
33	|---|---|---|
34	| Memory transport | Shared `/dev/shm` file mmap'd by QEMU1, vsim, QEMU2 via `-object memory-backend-file,share=on,...`. Zero-copy. | `dump-guest-memory` -> ELF core -> `tools/qemu_elfdump_to_main_memory.sh` extracts PT_LOAD 0 -> gzip -> vsim `--restore-memory <gz>`. |
35	| Arch state format | Binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct in `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`. Magic + version + ABI-locked offsets; layout enforced by `state_abi_check.h` static_asserts. | Text file `ae350regs.txt` with `REG`/`CSR`/`MMIO` lines; converted by `tools/regs2cmds.sh` into a GDB script of `set $csrN = 0x...` commands. |
36	| Drain mechanism | QEMU TCG plugin `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` triggered on `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` or on ELF-symbol PC. Programmatic, no human in the loop. | Manual rendezvous on WFI: `Ctrl-A c` for `dump-guest-memory`, then attach GDB and `source tools/dump_ae350.gdb`. |
37	| Restore mechanism | vsim `ResumeDriver` (DMI Abstract Commands + Program Buffer); for QEMU2, `qemu_handback` spawns QEMU2 and pushes registers via gdbstub P-packets. | `./sim --restore-memory snap --reset-vector PC`, then attach GDB and `source ae350regs.cmds`, `set $dpc`, `continue`. |
38	| V extension support | Yes. V regs go through scratch GPA `0x80FF0000` via `vse8.v`; vtype/vl restored via Program Buffer `vsetvl`; vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr via Abstract Cmds. | Not supported. `dump_ae350.gdb` lists only Andes V5 CSRs - no V regs and no V CSRs. |
39	| Trigger surface | `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1` (default) or ELF-symbol PC (`_hybrid_enter_pc`/`_hybrid_exit_pc`). Both extensible from the TCG plugin (insn-count, region marker, ...). | WFI only; manual UI driving. Extending requires GDB scripting or QMP scripting. |
40	| Per-handoff latency | Microseconds: mmap is shared (no copy); state file is a few KB binary. | Seconds: 2 GiB gzip pass + ELF parsing + GDB scripting per drain and per restore. |
41	| Coupling between sides | Tight - both sides include the same C ABI header. | Loose - the GDB remote protocol is the only contract. |
42	| Auditability of snapshot | Binary; needs a viewer (or a converter to text). | Human-readable `ae350regs.txt` is the wire format. Easy to diff. |
43	| Persistence model | One live mmap file at a time; ephemeral. Snapshotting per region is `cp` (reflink-friendly). | One snapshot *directory* per checkpoint; archivable, portable, by construction. |
44	
45	Key file references in `hybrid_sim`:
46	
47	- `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (wire struct)
48	- `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (drain on QEMU side; natural home for BBV emission too)
49	- `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (restore into vsim via DMI)
50	- `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` (drain on vsim side)
51	- `tests/e2e.sh` (tier-2 harness using `memory-backend-file`)
52	
53	Key file references in the demo:
54	
55	- `demo/hybrid/main.c` (WFI-trigger fixture)
56	- `demo/hybrid/tools/dump_ae350.gdb` (GDB script that prints `ae350regs.txt`)
57	- `demo/hybrid/tools/regs2cmds.sh` (text -> GDB restore commands)
58	- `demo/hybrid/tools/qemu_elfdump_to_main_memory.sh` (ELF core -> gz raw)
59	- `demo/hybrid/README.md` (step-by-step instructions, ~140 lines)
60	
61	---
62	
63	## 2. Fit to a SimPoint pipeline driven from QEMU
64	
65	SimPoint needs three things from the host simulator:
66	
67	- **BBV emission**: per fixed-size slice (e.g. every 100 M insns), count how
68	  many times each static basic block was executed; dump as one row of the
69	  `.bb` file.
70	- **Insn-count trigger**: fire a drain when the dynamic instruction counter
71	  reaches a SimPoint-chosen value.
72	- **K-region replay**: K snapshots persisted to disk, each independently
73	  restorable.
74	
75	### 2.1 Shared mmap
76	
77	Strengths:
78	
79	- **BBV emission lives in the same plugin as the drain hook.** The QEMU TCG
80	  plugin already sees every translated TB and every executed insn; counting
81	  per-BB hits per slice and writing a row to a `.bb` file is a natural
82	  extension of `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`. No new process, no GDB.
83	- **Insn-count trigger is a one-line addition** to the existing CSR/PC
84	  trigger logic in the plugin. The plugin already runs at retire time.
85	- **Per-snapshot drain is microseconds.** Taking K=10 (or K=30) checkpoints
86	  is effectively free relative to the simulation work.
87	- **Memory snapshot per region is a file copy of the mmap backing**:
88	  `cp --reflink=auto /dev/shm/mem snap/N/mem`. On btrfs/xfs this is
89	  O(metadata). On other filesystems it is one sequential read+write of RAM
90	  size, no compression on the critical path.
91	- **vsim restore path is unchanged.** `ResumeDriver` does not care whether
92	  `hybrid_state_v1` was emitted at a WFI, a CSR write, or an insn-count
93	  boundary.
94	- **V-state already validated end to end** through `rt_c_v_regs`,
95	  `rt_c_v_csrs` fixtures. SimPoint-driven runs of V workloads inherit this.
96	
97	Weaknesses:
98	
99	- A shared mmap is *live*. To collect K checkpoints we need to copy the
100	  mmap to a per-region file as part of the drain step; that is one extra
101	  syscall in the plugin but it must happen *before* QEMU resumes mutating
102	  the mmap. Solvable in the plugin (it is already the synchronization
103	  point) but a new code path.
104	- The binary ABI couples both sides: when state grows (new CSR, wider VLEN)
105	  the header bumps and producer + consumer rebuild in lock-step.
106	- vsim today reads memory live from the mmap. For checkpoint *replay* we
107	  need vsim to mmap the per-region snapshot file instead of the live one.
108	  This is a flag change in the tier-2 harness (`--shared-mem-path
109	  snap/N/mem`), not a structural change.
110	
111	### 2.2 Dump/reload
112	
113	Strengths:
114	
115	- Snapshots are *directories on disk* by construction. K checkpoints, K
116	  directories, no extra copy step.
117	- Loose coupling: schema drift between QEMU and vsim is absorbed in the awk
118	  filter (`void` and read-only entries are dropped).
119	- Human-readable text dump is a great debugging aid for a single mismatched
120	  CSR.
121	
122	Weaknesses:
123	
124	- **No BBV story.** GDB cannot see per-TB execution counts; `dump-guest-memory`
125	  is a memory dump, not an instrumentation hook. BBV emission would have to
126	  go in a TCG plugin anyway, at which point we are back to the mmap design
127	  for the BBV side and only using dump/reload for the snapshot side.
128	- **No insn-count trigger.** WFI is the only rendezvous today; reaching a
129	  SimPoint boundary by WFI would require injecting WFI traps into the
130	  workload, which is invasive and slow.
131	- **Per-region wall time is dominated by gzip of memory and GDB
132	  serialization.** For K=10 phases over a 2 GiB image, this is roughly two
133	  minutes of pure I/O per replay before any simulation begins.
134	- **V regs and V CSRs not supported.** Extending the text dump to cover them
135	  re-invents the V-state transport that the mmap path already has working.
136	- **GDB-as-orchestrator** means three or four shell processes per snapshot
137	  (QEMU, ICEman or vsim's gdbstub, GDB, vsim itself). Hard to make reliable
138	  across K regions in CI.
139	
140	### 2.3 Cost summary on a 2 GiB workload, K=10 regions
141	
142	| Stage | Shared mmap | Dump/reload |
143	|---|---|---|
144	| BBV emission (whole run) | in-plugin counter, one fwrite per slice (microseconds) | not natively supported; would need a parallel plugin anyway |
145	| Drain (per region) | ~0.05 ms (`state.bin` write) + cp/reflink of mmap | ~30 s (gzip 2 GiB) + ~2 s (GDB script) |
146	| Snapshot to disk (per region) | ~3 s `cp`, ~0 with reflink | already on disk |
147	| Restore into vsim (per region) | ~10 ms (DMI replay) + mmap open of snap | ~20 s (gunzip) + ~5 s (GDB replay) |
148	| Total per region | ~3 s worst case, ~10 ms with reflink | ~55 s |
149	| Total for K=10 | ~30 s worst case | ~10 min |
150	
151	Numbers are order-of-magnitude estimates, not measured. The point is the gap
152	is one to three decades, not 2x.
153	
154	---
155	
156	## 3. Recommendation
157	
158	Adopt the shared-mmap transport. Extend the existing TCG plugin and tier-2
159	harness; do not introduce the dump/reload path.
160	
161	### 3.1 What changes in `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`
162	
163	1. **Add a BBV-emit mode** (`bbv_out=<path>,slice=<N>` plugin args). On each
164	   executed TB, increment a `bbv_t -> count` map keyed by translation-time
165	   BB id; every `slice` retired insns, write one row to the `.bb` file and
166	   reset the map. This is the standard SimPoint input format.
167	2. **Add an insn-count trigger** (`drain_at=<csv-of-N>` plugin arg). When the
168	   retired-insn counter reaches each value, run the same drain code path
169	   that the existing CSR/PC triggers use, and emit `state.bin` + the memory
170	   snapshot under `snap/region_<N>/`. The drain code already exists; only
171	   the trigger is new.
172	3. **Memory snapshot at drain time**: in the plugin, immediately before
173	   returning to QEMU, `cp --reflink=auto` (or plain `read/write`) the live
174	   mmap to `snap/region_<N>/mem`. This is the only new I/O code path.
175	
176	### 3.2 What changes in vsim
177	
178	Nothing structural. The tier-2 harness already accepts `--shared-mem-path`,
179	`--shared-mem-size`, `--shared-mem-base`. For replay, point it at
180	`snap/region_N/mem` and `--resume-from-qemu snap/region_N/state.bin`.
181	`ResumeDriver` is unchanged.
182	
183	### 3.3 What to keep from the demo
184	
185	The one feature worth borrowing is the **text pretty-printer** for snapshots.
186	Port `regs2cmds.sh` into a small tool that takes `hybrid_state_v1` (binary)
187	and prints `REG`/`CSR`/`MMIO` lines. Useful for diffing region N vs region N+1
188	when something looks wrong. Not on the critical path; ships alongside
189	snapshots as optional `state.txt`.
190	
191	### 3.4 What to drop from the demo entirely
192	
193	- gzip + ELF extraction of memory
194	- WFI as the only trigger
195	- text-as-wire-format
196	- GDB as the restore driver
197	
198	They were appropriate for a manual one-shot demo; they are wrong for
199	K-region replay.
200	
201	### 3.5 Final snapshot tree
202	
203	```
204	snap/
205	  bbv.bb                     # SimPoint input
206	  simpoints.txt              # SimPoint output (chosen region indices + weights)
207	  region_00/
208	    mem                      # mmap snapshot, restorable via memory-backend-file
209	    state.bin                # hybrid_state_v1
210	    state.txt                # optional pretty-print
211	  region_01/
212	    mem
213	    state.bin
214	    state.txt
215	  ...
216	```
217	
218	Each `region_N/` is independently consumable by the existing tier-2 harness.
219	
220	---
221	
222	## 4. Open questions before we commit
223	
224	- **Slice size for BBV emission**: SimPoint papers commonly use 100 M
225	  insns; we should sanity-check that against our workload lengths and
226	  cluster stability.
227	- **Insn counting precision in the plugin**: QEMU's
228	  `qemu_plugin_register_vcpu_insn_exec_cb` fires per executed insn but
229	  may batch by TB; the exact retire-time counter that the drain reads must
230	  match the one the trigger compares against, or we drift across regions.
231	- **Multi-hart workloads**: BBVs and checkpoints are per-hart. Decide
232	  whether to extend `hybrid_state_v1` to multiple harts in the same file
233	  or to one file per hart per region.
234	- **Snapshot warmup**: cycle-accurate replay needs cache/TLB/branch-predictor
235	  warmup before the measurement window opens. Neither transport addresses
236	  this today; it belongs in a separate doc.
237	- **Region length for detailed sim**: Verilator throughput sets a practical
238	  upper bound on N (insns per measured region). We should benchmark vsim
239	  on a representative workload before fixing N in the SimPoint clustering.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives the handoff; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    csr | pc (default csr).
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-csr}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  csr) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    ENTER_PC=$(printf '%s\n' "$NM_OUT" | awk '$3=="_hybrid_enter_pc"{print $1}')
    EXIT_PC=$(printf '%s\n' "$NM_OUT"  | awk '$3=="_hybrid_exit_pc"{print $1}')
    if [ -z "${ENTER_PC:-}" ] || [ -z "${EXIT_PC:-}" ]; then
      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE pc]: missing _hybrid_enter_pc/_hybrid_exit_pc symbols"
      exit 1
    fi
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use csr|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

# Opt-in: mcycle/minstret must strictly increase from QEMU 1's drain
# to vsim's drain. Offsets locked by state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624,
# minstret@632). Runs before the RC gate so the verdict is independent
# of any downstream failure.
if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ] && [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ]; then
  read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
  echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
  echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
  if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
    exit 1
  fi
  if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
fi

# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
# Anything else is a hard failure: the run is only complete when vsim
# drained cleanly.
if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  exit 1
fi

if [ ! -s "$STATE_VSIM" ]; then
  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim did not produce a drained state file"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

/* Drain markers shared by all C-level round-trip fixtures.
 *
 * Phase rule:
 *   The span between enter_vsim() and exit_vsim()
 *   runs on vsim and MUST NOT issue any syscall. Newlib stdio (printf,
 *   fputs, fwrite, ...) bottoms out in libgloss_vh's semihosting magic
 *   triple, which is intercepted by QEMU but not by vsim -- inside the
 *   span the triple would route to mtvec and loop. Phase 2 is restricted
 *   to register/memory work only.
 *
 *   Printing is permitted in QEMU1 (before enter_vsim) and in
 *   QEMU2 (after exit_vsim) via standard newlib stdio. Both
 *   QEMU launches set -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native.
 */

#ifndef RT_C_HELPERS_H
#define RT_C_HELPERS_H

/* Plugin- / handoff-controller-recognized drain markers (CSR 0x7C0,
 * uimm 0 = ENTER, uimm 1 = EXIT). Match insn_match.h.
 *
 * Each helper exposes a global `_hybrid_{enter,exit}_pc` label co-located
 * with the csrwi insn. The labels are inert in CSR mode and consumed by
 * the PC-trigger mode driver (resolved via `nm --defined-only`). Because
 * each fixture calls each helper exactly once, the labels stay unique. */
/* The "memory" clobber forces the compiler to spill all globals to memory
 * across the marker and reload them after, since vsim's drain+resume is
 * (from the compiler's POV) an opaque event that could observe or alter
 * any memory. Without it, the compiler may hoist global-pointer arithmetic
 * (e.g. &_impure_ptr) into a callee-saved register across the marker and
 * use it after resume; if vsim doesn't faithfully restore that register
 * the post-resume code dereferences garbage. The clobber list deliberately
 * does NOT include GPRs: the round-trip is required to preserve them. */
/* Cycle-attribution contract (for cycle-measuring benchmarks):
 *
 * The "memory" clobber pins memory loads/stores across the marker but NOT
 * register-only computation. A vector kernel that keeps its inputs/outputs
 * in vector registers across the boundary can be hoisted before enter_vsim
 * or sunk after exit_vsim, charging its cycles to the wrong phase. (Tested
 * on the Andes GCC at -O2/-O3: an out-of-line marker does NOT help -- a
 * call only forces a register spill, not the position of the compute that
 * consumes the value.)
 *
 * To keep a kernel inside the measured window, anchor it through memory:
 *   - read its inputs from memory and write its outputs to memory INSIDE
 *     the span (the load cannot move before enter, the store cannot move
 *     after exit, and the compute is data-chained between them), or
 *   - put the kernel in its own __attribute__((noinline)) function called
 *     between the markers.
 * Both keep every kernel op in the ROI with zero annotation and zero
 * overhead. Carrying live vector values in registers across the boundary is
 * fine for CORRECTNESS (all regs round-trip) -- rt_c_v_regs.c does exactly
 * that (relying on the compiler keeping x in a V register across the
 * boundary) as the V-regfile TRANSPORT test -- but it is not safe for cycle
 * attribution. */
static inline void enter_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl _hybrid_enter_pc\n"
                       "_hybrid_enter_pc:\n"
                       "csrwi 0x7C0, 0\n" ::: "memory");
}
static inline void exit_vsim(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__(".globl _hybrid_exit_pc\n"
                       "_hybrid_exit_pc:\n"
                       "csrwi 0x7C0, 1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* RT_C_HELPERS_H */

# All fixtures share test.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# against the Andes virtual-hosting libgloss (libgloss_vh.a), which
# implements _write / _exit / _sbrk / _read / ... via the RISC-V
# semihosting magic triple. QEMU1 and QEMU2 are launched with
# -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native and intercept the triple
# before it reaches mtvec. vsim does not implement semihosting -- phase
# 2 (the span between enter_vsim and exit_vsim)
# is therefore syscall-free by rule (see runtime/rt_c_helpers.h).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_no_trigger_exit
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul
# Probe fixtures: QEMU1-only, no vsim/QEMU2 phase. Used by shell tests
# that inspect the raw state file to verify plugin drain behavior.

input.old_string:
### Three-Phase Handoff

```
QEMU1 --(state file)--> vsim --(state file + V-scratch mmap)--> QEMU2
```

1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On CSR-write trigger (`csrwi 0x7C0, 0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands.
5. **qemu_handback** (`src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp`) - Spawns QEMU2, connects via gdbstub, sends P-packet register writes for GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-regs, then `continue`s.

**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes only the CSRs that the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret`. The QEMU plugin still drains the full M-mode set (`mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`) plus PMP (64 `pmpaddr` + 16 `pmpcfg`) into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are restored only on QEMU2 via the gdbstub P-packet path in `qemu_handback`. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

### Two-Phase Handoff

```
QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
```

1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On CSR-write trigger (`csrwi 0x7C0, 0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs/CSRs/V-state into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands and Program Buffer.
4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg (gdbstub P-packet restore into a freshly spawned QEMU) was removed entirely.

**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes only the CSRs that the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mcycle`, `minstret`. The QEMU plugin still drains the full M-mode set (`mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, `satp`) plus PMP (64 `pmpaddr` + 16 `pmpcfg`) into `hybrid_state_v1`, but those are not restored anywhere -- they remain in the struct as the drained record only. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

small region-of-interest at cycle accuracy. They share RAM via an

hands control between them. One run is three legs:

   (fast)                                 (cycle accurate)         (fast)
```

The thing you choose per run is the TRIGGER that decides where each
leg drains and the next leg resumes. That choice is the "switching
mode".

The hybrid simulator runs a program across two phases:

```

A "switching mode" is the RULE that decides WHEN each leg drains its

# Out-of-tree build for the QEMU TCG plugin libhybrid_handoff.so. Standalone
# from the vsim CMake build because the plugin links against host QEMU's
# headers + glib, neither of which exist inside the vsim build container.
#
# Usage:
#   make QEMU_ROOT=/local/nick/qemu_v5
#
# Output: libhybrid_handoff.so in this directory.

QEMU_ROOT ?= /local/nick/qemu_v5
CC        ?= gcc

GLIB_CFLAGS := $(shell pkg-config --cflags glib-2.0)
GLIB_LIBS   := $(shell pkg-config --libs   glib-2.0)

CFLAGS  := -O2 -fPIC -Wall -Wextra -std=c11
HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include
INCLUDES := -I$(HYBRID_INCLUDE) -I$(QEMU_ROOT)/include/qemu $(GLIB_CFLAGS)
LDFLAGS := -shared
LIBS    := $(GLIB_LIBS)

 ## Repository Overview
 
-Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a three-phase round-trip: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain) -> **QEMU2** (restore via gdbstub, continue).
+Andes hybrid RISC-V co-simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a two-phase handoff: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta; there is no QEMU2 leg (the vsim->QEMU2 handback was removed -- the run ends at the vsim drain).
 
 Two Git submodules:
 - `QEMU/` - QEMU fork hosting the TCG plugin (branch: `hybrid`)
@@ -68,19 +68,18 @@ LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs bash scripts/run_e2e.sh    # custom log directory
 
 ## Architecture
 
-### Three-Phase Handoff
+### Two-Phase Handoff
 
 ```
-QEMU1 --(state file)--> vsim --(state file + V-scratch mmap)--> QEMU2
+QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
 ```
